items.title: Rebondissement sur l’affaire de l’assassinat de l’inspecteur Sabo Adama à Nouna: Le militaire écroué déjoue la surveillance pénitentiaire pour s’évader
items.description: L'affaire de l'assassinat de l'inspecteur Sabo Adama, mortellement touché par balle à son domicile le 5 octobre 2026 à Nouna, connaît un rebondissement sécuritaire majeur. Le principal suspect, Wendlassida Philippe Koama, un militaire du rang de 22 ans inculpé et placé sous mandat de dépôt le 9 octobre, s'est évadé de la Maison d'arrêt et de correction de Nouna (MACN) le 22 octobre après avoir rusé avec ses gardes. Face à cette fuite, les autorités pénitentiaires et judiciaires ont lancé un avis de recherche officiel et appellent la population à la vigilance pour permettre l'interpellation rapide du prévenu. L'émotion demeure vive au sein du milieu éducatif et parmi les habitants de Nouna. Le 5 octobre 2026, l'inspecteur Sabo Adama a été tué par balle à son domicile, suscitant une vive onde de choc dans la province de la Kossi. Les investigations immédiatement engagées par les services de justice ont conduit à l'interpellation, le 9 octobre 2026, de Wendlassida Philippe Koama, un soldat du rang âgé de 22 ans et domicilié à Nouna. Mis en examen pour assassinat, le jeune militaire avait été placé sous mandat de dépôt par le juge d'instruction du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Nouna. Alors que l'instruction suivait son cours, la procédure a pris une tournure inattendue. Le 22 octobre 2026, le détenu est parvenu à s'échapper de la Maison d'arrêt et de correction de Nouna. Selon les éléments du communiqué officiel, Wendlassida Philippe Koama a fait usage de ruse pour tromper la vigilance de la garde pénitentiaire. Né le 1ᵉʳ janvier 2004 à Lao et mesurant 1,61 m, le fugitif fait désormais l'objet d'une traque active engagée par l'ensemble des forces de la puissance publique. En raison de la gravité des faits et des risques pour la sécurité publique, les autorités ont diffusé un avis de recherche généralisé. Le document officiel précise qu'en cas de localisation ou d'interpellation, le fugitif doit être immédiatement conduit devant le directeur de la Maison d'arrêt et de correction de Nouna, le procureur du Faso près le TGI de Nouna ou le juge d'instruction saisi du dossier. Eu égard au profil du suspect poursuivi pour un crime de sang, les autorités recommandent fermement aux citoyens de ne tenter aucune interpellation individuelle et d'alerter sans délai les services compétents. items.title: Tragédie scolaire à Dano : Décès de Élodie Somé, meilleure fille au BAC D 2026 du Ioba
items.description: La communauté éducative du Ioba et les habitants de la commune de Dano sont plongés dans le deuil suite au décès de la camarade SOMÉ Élodie. Élève brillante du Lycée provincial polyvalent du Ioba, elle s'était illustrée en obtenant le titre de meilleure fille au baccalauréat série D (session de 2026) dans la commune. Orientée en pharmacie et candidate engagée à la compétition Akili Mousso , la jeune défunte suscitait de grands espoirs par sa rigueur et son mérite académique. Alors que les funérailles se déroulent à Mebar, un hommage appuyé lui est rendu par l'ensemble des acteurs du monde éducatif. C'est avec une profonde douleur que la communauté éducative du Ioba a appris le décès de la camarade SOMÉ Élodie. Précédemment élève au Lycée provincial polyvalent du Ioba, la jeune fille s'était hissée au sommet des résultats scolaires en devenant la meilleure candidate féminine au baccalauréat série D de la session 2026 dans la commune de Dano. Sa réussite remarquable faisait la fierté de ses encadreurs et de ses camarades de promotion. Reconnue pour ses qualités intellectuelles et son ardeur au travail, Élodie Somé se préparait à embrasser une carrière dans la santé. Orientée en pharmacie, elle s'était également portée candidate à la compétition Akili Mousso , une initiative valorisant le potentiel et les compétences de la jeune fille. Son profil prometteur et ses ambitions académiques suscitaient une grande admiration au sein de sa communauté. En cette douloureuse circonstance, la communauté éducative du Ioba a adressé ses condoléances les plus attristées à la famille éplorée, aux proches ainsi qu'à tous les élèves touchés par ce drame. Les cérémonies funèbres se déroulent dans la localité de Mebar, où la population est invitée à se mobiliser pour entourer et soutenir la famille endeuillée dans cette épreuve. 🕊️ Souhaitez-vous que nous préparions un projet de message de condoléances officiel pour la communauté éducative ou une brève d'information pour la radio ? items.title: Forêt de la NOAHO : le BIR 11 détruit deux campements terroristes
items.description: Le Onzième Bataillon d’Intervention Rapide (BIR 11) a mené une seconde action offensive dans la forêt de la NOAHO. Cette opération a permis de détruire deux campements de groupes terroristes et de récupérer un important lot de matériel. Selon le bilan , plusieurs combattants ont été neutralisés, tandis que d’autres ont pris la fuite. Côté ami, aucun incident n’a été signalé. Le matériel récupéré comprend notamment une mitrailleuse PKMS, un pistolet artisanal, quatre bandes de 100 cartouches pour PKMS, trois chargeurs garnis d’AK-47, treize téléphones portables et deux postes radio TYT. Cinq têtes de chèvres, des documents, des textes coraniques et divers vivres ont également été retrouvés. Deux motos et quatre vélos ont été détruits sur place. Les vivres, les matériels de couchage et divers produits pharmaceutiques ont été brûlés au cours de l’opération. Cette seconde offensive porte un coup aux capacités logistiques des groupes armés opérant dans cette zone. items.title: Ouagadougou : près de quatre cents usagers interpellés en trois heures lors d’un contrôle nocturne du port du casque
items.description: Près de quatre cents usagers ont été interpellés en seulement trois heures, dans la nuit du vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, lors d'une opération de contrôle visant ceux qui abandonnent le port du casque à la tombée de la nuit. Cette sortie qui entre dans le cadre de l’opération « Bouclier tête durcie », répond à un constat des services de police : une fois la nuit tombée, certains usagers délaissent le casque, pourtant obligatoire. Pour s'assurer de l'effectivité de la mesure aux heures nocturnes, le directeur régional de la Police nationale du Kadiogo (DRPN-K), le contrôleur général de police Aguima Abdoulaziz Yonli, a effectué une sortie de terrain dans les artères de la ville. Il était accompagné du commissaire central de police de la ville de Ouagadougou, commissaire principal de police Hamado Tassembédo et du commandant de la Brigade anti-criminalité, commissaire Principal de police Moïse Kaboré. La délégation a parcouru plusieurs carrefours stratégiques de la capitale. Selon le bilan communiqué par les chefs de postes des dispositifs de contrôle déployés à cet effet, près de quatre cents usagers ont été interpellés au cours des trois heures d'opération. À l'issue du contrôle, le DRPN-K a invité les usagers de la route à porter systématiquement le casque, de jour comme de nuit, et à en faire un réflexe pour préserver leur vie. « On n'a pas une tête de secours à la maison, on n'en a qu'une seule et nous devons la protéger. Si nous le faisons, c'est d'abord pour notre propre bien et ensuite pour celui de notre famille. Protégeons nos vies », a-t-il martelé. Le contrôleur général Yonli a également félicité et encouragé les agents mobilisés pour les résultats obtenus et le professionnalisme dont ils font preuve dans l'accomplissement de leurs missions. Source : DCRP Police nationale L’article Ouagadougou : près de quatre cents usagers interpellés en trois heures lors d'un contrôle nocturne du port du casque est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: We do not support our own, but we watch horrible Hollywood movies – Yvonne Okoro
items.description: Ghanaian actor and film producer Yvonne Okoro has bemoaned the lack of support for local films. Speaking to Kwame Dadzie on Joy FM’s Showbiz A-Z , Yvonne said that while Ghanaian film producers were doing their best to survive, local audiences often looked for faults in their work rather than supporting their productions. According to her, Ghanaians would watch and enjoy poor-quality films from other countries but criticise similar productions made by their compatriots. “We do not support our own. Everything Ghanaian, we see it as sub-standard. And when you say this, people get offended by it, but it’s the truth,” she said. “Like, you do a movie, and people are like, will the movie be nice? You are watching horrible movies. I am sorry, some Hollywood movies are horrible. You watch it and clap. “You are watching some of the YouTube videos from my people in Nigeria, and you think it’s fantastic. But then let it be a Ghanaian who does a horrible movie, and they will say we don’t know how to do good movies. “It’s horrible. And when we do good movies, they will go like, ‘I didn’t know this was there oo.’ I have been marketing for how long now; you didn’t know this was there. They just won’t come and watch it,” she added. Yvonne made the remarks during a discussion on the current state of Ghana’s film industry and what could be done to improve it. Yvonne has built a career spanning acting and film production, featuring in several Ghanaian and Ghanaian-Nigerian productions. Her acting credits include Beyonce: The President’s Daughter, The Return of Beyonce, Single Six, Contract, Potomanto, Rebecca, Ghana Must Go, Like Cotton Twines and Fix Us. She has also appeared in the Adams Apples film series, which explores the lives and relationships of a group of friends. As a producer, Yvonne has worked on films including Contract and Ghana Must Go , demonstrating her involvement in both the creative and production sides of the industry. She recently starred in Agency for the Dead , a new film by Ghanaian filmmaker Shirley Frimpong-Manso, hitting Silverbird Cinemas on 30th October 2026.

items.title: Parc Thomas SANKARA à Rome : bel exemple d’amitié entre le Burkina Faso et l’Italie
items.description: L’image du Père de la Révolution burkinabè trône officiellement à compter de ce samedi 24 octobre 2026, au sein d’un parc dans la municipalité de l’arrondissement 3 de Rome, en Italie. Un prisme en acier mesurant 2m de haut et 70 cm de largeur, taillé à l’effigie du Capitaine Thomas SANKARA en plein cœur de la capitale italienne, traduisant l’amitié et la fraternité entre deux peuples, dont les idéaux du Capitaine SANKARA ont su réunir. Cet édifice offert par le Camarade Madi SAKANDE et réalisé par l’artiste Hamed Sékou OUATTARA, a été inauguré par le ministre en charge de la Culture, le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO avec à ses côtés les ambassadeurs du Burkina Faso à Rome, la Camarade Cyrille GANOU/BADOLO et au Vatican, le Camarade Régis Kevin BATIONO et entouré d’une diaspora burkinabè et de l’AES fortement mobilisée. Plusieurs représentants des Missions diplomatiques accrédités à Rome et au Saint Siège dont les ambassadeurs du Mali et du Niger ont aussi pris part à la cérémonie d’inauguration. Pour le président de la municipalité de l’arrondissement 3 de Rome, l’inauguration du parc Thomas SANKARA, baptisé le 17 septembre 2025, vise à créer un pont entre deux terres éloignées géographiquement mais proche dans leur définition de l’humanité comme le préconisait le Capitaine Thomas SANKARA. Un exemple concret de fraternité qui permettra, selon Monsieur Paolo Emilio MARCHIONNE, de perpétuer les idéaux du Président SANKARA en mettant en avant la fraternité et le dialogue entre les peuples. l’Ambassadeur Cyrille GANOU/BADOLO a exprimé sa gratitude aux autorités burkinabè d’avoir offert cette tribune à sa juridiction pour remercier les autorités italiennes pour le choix porté sur le Capitaine Thomas SANKARA. Elle a indiqué que cette célébration prouve une fois de plus que le Père de la Révolution burkinabè «n’appartient à aucun pays ni à aucune génération, il appartient à toute l’humanité». Elle a invité la jeune génération à poursuivre l’œuvre de transformation et de responsabilité incarnée par le Capitaine SANKARA. Cette initiative qui a brisé les distances entre deux peuples, «enseigne au monde et à l’humanité que le combat pour la dignité, la justice et l’émancipation des peuples est un combat universel et intemporel», a déclaré le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO. «La où Rome rappelle à l’humanité ce que fut la puissance Thomas SANKARA à travers ce parc, rappellera dorénavant au monde ce que représente la force des idées», soutient le ministre de la Culture. Témoignant du sens de l’hospitalité du peuple italien, le ministre chargé de la Culture a relevé la réciprocité d’exemption de visa entre le Burkina Faso et l’Italie pour les personnes en missions officielles dans l’un ou l’autre pays. «Si nous sommes rentrés sans visa chez vous, cela montre que nous sommes chez nous, et c’est ce combat que le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE défend et c'est de cette fraternité dont le monde a besoin» a-t-il souligné. Au cours de la cérémonie, le camarade ministre de la culture a officiellement lancé la campagne internationale de collecte de Fonds pour le projet de construction du mémorial Thomas SANKARA, dénommée «une brique pour SANKARA». Notons que le parc Thomas SANKARA a vu le jour grâce au dévouement d’un jeune italien du nom de Matteo Pietro SANTE qui, s'appuyant sur l'engagement de Thomas-SANKARA, a contribué à mobiliser les autorités italiennes autour de ce projet. DCRP/MAE L’article Parc Thomas SANKARA à Rome : bel exemple d’amitié entre le Burkina Faso et l’Italie est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Ghana loses GH¢209.7m to cyber incidents in nine months – CSA
items.description: Ghana recorded an estimated GH¢209.7 million in losses from reported cybersecurity incidents between January and September 2026, the Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Dr Divine Selasi Agbeti, has disclosed. The Authority recorded 4,938 incidents during the period. This compares with 4,604 incidents and reported losses of more than GH¢22.5 million in 2025. Speaking at the fifth annual Cyber Secure Volta Regional Conference in Ho, Dr Agbeti described the figures as worrying. He urged individuals, businesses and public institutions to strengthen their cybersecurity practices. He cautioned that the reported cases did not capture the full scale of the problem. Some victims, he said, remained reluctant to report incidents because of embarrassment, fear of ridicule and other concerns. Dr Agbeti encouraged victims of online fraud, blackmail, cyberbullying and extortion to report their experiences to the appropriate authorities. He explained that reporting would support investigations and help prevent further victimisation. He said human error and social engineering accounted for a significant proportion of incidents, making public education and responsible online behaviour essential. The CSA plans to establish an office in the Volta Region before the end of 2026 to support law enforcement and strengthen the local response to cybercrime. Dr Agbeti said the government and the Authority were committed to preventing Ghana from becoming a haven for cybercriminals. He noted that arrests and prosecutions had been pursued since 2025, including operations in the Volta Region. He urged residents to report suspected criminal activity and cautioned against allowing their communities to become hiding places for cybercriminals. Landlords were advised to make reasonable enquiries before renting out their properties. Members of the public can also report suspected cybercrime through the CSA’s short code, 292 , which he said operates around the clock. Turning to digital financial services, Dr Agbeti warned mobile money, internet banking and digital wallet users to be wary of suspicious investment offers and promises of unrealistic returns. He also cautioned against transferring money to unfamiliar accounts and urged users to verify payment requests before authorising transactions. He said protecting passwords and other sensitive information remained essential to reducing exposure to online fraud.

items.title: Le dirham s'apprécie de 0,61% face au dollar du 15 au 21 octobre
items.description: Le dirham s'est apprécié de 0,61% face au dollar américain et de 0,17% vis-à-vis de l'euro durant la période du 15 au 21 octobre 2026, selon Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM). Au cours de cette période, aucune opération d'adjudication n'a été réalisée sur le marché des changes, indique BAM dans son récent bulletin des indicateurs hebdomadaires. Les avoirs officiels de réserve se sont établis à 510,2 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au 16 octobre, en baisse de 1% par rapport à la semaine précédente et en hausse de 18,8% en glissement annuel. Concernant les interventions de BAM, elles ont totalisé, au cours de la même période, 147,2 MMDH en moyenne quotidienne. Ce volume se répartit entre des avances à 7 jours pour 51,8 MMDH, des pensions livrées à plus long terme pour 44,9 MMDH ainsi que des prêts garantis pour 50,5 MMDH. Sur le marché interbancaire, le volume quotidien moyen des échanges s'est établi à 3 MMDH et le taux interbancaire s'est situé à 2,25%. Lors de l'appel d'offres du 21 octobre (date de valeur le 22 octobre), la Banque centrale a injecté un montant de 50,6 MMDH sous forme d'avances à 7 jours. Côté Bourse, le MASI s'est apprécié de 0,2%, ramenant sa contre-performance depuis le début de l'année à -9,8%. Cette évolution reflète notamment des hausses de 8,4% pour l'indice de la « Participation et promotion immobilières », de 0,8% pour celui des « Banques », de 2,1% pour les « Services de transport » et de 1,1% pour les « Mines ». En revanche, les indices des « Bâtiment et matériaux de construction » et des « Télécommunications » ont enregistré des baisses respectives de 2,2% et 2,9%. Pour ce qui est du volume hebdomadaire des échanges, il est revenu, d'une semaine à l'autre, de 0,9 MMDH à 0,8 MMDH, réalisé principalement sur le marché central actions. items.title: Omitted candidates: PDP, ADC, NDC, LP meet INEC’s condition
items.description: •INEC to clarify omitted candidate’s status this week By Henry Umoru, John Alechenu, Luminous Jannamike & Emma Una ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, has met the Independent National Electoral Commission’s, INEC, October 24 deadline for correcting the names of candidates omitted from its published list, the party’s National Organising Secretary, Captain Umar Bature, retd, has said. Read Also: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi The party’s governorship candidates in Ogun(Oladipupo Adebutu), and Gombe(Prof Isa Pantanmi) and seven House of Assembly candidates were omitted in the list published by the electoral umpire, recently. Apart from the PDP, other opposition parties such as the Social Democratic Party, SDP; Nigeria democratic Congress, NDC; African Democratic Congress, ADC; and Action Democratic Party, ADP; and Labour Party, LP, were also affected. The INEC gave the affected parties October 24 as deadline to correct the omissions. The affected candidates include governorship hopefuls in Gombe and Ogun states, as well as about six or seven House of Assembly candidates, whose names were missing from the list released by the electoral commission. Bature confirmed the development, yesterday, in a response to Vanguard, saying the PDP completed the corrections within the stipulated period. “Yes, we met the deadline since,” he said. NDC, ADP meet INEC deadline on omitted candidates Also, the National Leadership of the NDC said it met the INEC’s deadline for correcting the names of candidates omitted from the published list. When Vanguard sought to know if the party has met the deadline, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director simply said, “ Yes, we did.” Similarly, the National leadership of the ADP said it met the deadline. Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, the National Chairman of the ADP, Engr. Yabagi Yusuf Sani,said, “we did. Thanks a lot.” LP in good standing with INEC — Asogwa in like manner, the National Publicity Secretary of the LP, Ken Asogwa, said the party is in good standing with the INEC on correction of names and replacement of candidates. His words: “The Labour Party is in good standing with INEC, including on matters relating to the correction of names and replacement of candidates,” adding that the party is confident and looks forward to a successful outing for all its candidates in the forthcoming general elections. INEC’s clarification awaited The electoral umpire has not released additional information on the status of the omitted candidates especially those NDC’s John Upan and Ambassador Nkoyo Toyo of ADC in Cross River State Ambassador Toyo told Vanguard that she had done all that was needed to be done before the deadline expired but INEC is yet to bring out the result. “They gave us the deadline of October 24 which was Saturday and I had done all that they asked for but they have not brought out any information. Let’s wait for them” Contacted, the Head, INEC Voter Education in Cross River , Mr Osaro Aisen, said: “The whole thing is handled from Abuja and it is a legal matter. Let’s see what will come forth tomorrow (Monday). “I cannot give you a categorical answer now till tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post Omitted candidates: PDP, ADC, NDC, LP meet INEC’s condition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan’s global role
items.description: THE nature of Pakistan’s role in global politics is once again the subject of much debate. Several officials are ferrying messages between Iran and the US for an end to the conflict, having helped organise a short-lived peace agreement earlier in the year. Based on these and past events, there are a series of judgement calls that observers make about the Pakistani state and its position in the world order. One set of views sees Pakistan as a client state of the US, that is, one that’s subservient to America’s imperial interests and its immediate allies in the region, the Gulf monarchies. This view is shared by sections of the left — globally, in the region, and within Pakistan — and disgruntled opponents of the current regime, who furnish as evidence for it the country’s role in global anti-communist politics in the 1950s and 1960s, its partnership with the US against the Soviets in Afghanistan, its role during the ‘war on terror’ between 2001 and 2013, and the proximity of ties with the Trump administration in recent months. Ironically, conservatives and Islamists also cite the 1950s/1960s and the experience of US-Pakistan relations during the war on terror and especially in the last few years, as evidence of successive regimes siding with global secularist interests in subjugating both Islamic movements in the region and Muslim political identity at home. The other view, held in the same time-space continuum, sees the country as ideologically fundamentalist, and simultaneously, a client of China and an unpredictable ally of the US — one that is capable of undermining the global hegemon on its own or in collaboration with the Chinese. This view is shared by much of the American and Indian mainstream, who cite CPEC and close military relations as an example of Chinese clientelism, previous support to the Taliban during the invasion of Afghanistan as an example of duplicity, and its approach to Kashmir, its recent diplomatic support for Iran, and the broader sociocultural and ideational life of its citizens, as an example of (religious) fundamentalism. As with most sweeping observations, many may detect a kernel of truth in these otherwise clearly contradictory positions. Close proximity to American imperial interests has characterised many passages in Pakistani political history. Similarly, the relationship with China remains remarkably consistent since the 1970s. However, in an effort to account for Pakistan’s global and regional behaviour, these observations lapse back to the rather broad and imprecise categories of ‘client state’ or ‘fundamentalist state’. The reality, just on the basis of the actions listed above, is that the state’s geopolitical and ideational positioning has varied considerably, which makes it hard to pin it down as a US ‘client’ of the same ilk as Japan/ South Korea or the Gulf monarchies, or as a Chinese client like North Korea. There are a series of judgement calls that observers make about the state’s position in the world order. What is consistent though is the subordinate role that the state here plays in global affairs, not just in terms of geopolitics but also — and more fundamentally — in terms of international economic processes. How does ‘subordinate’ differ from ‘client’? Beyond mere semantics, a substantive difference is that a subordinate actor may have limited agency, but it retains the capability of understanding and developing its own interests. A client, on the other hand, would, by and large replicate the interests of its patrons. On the evidence of the last seven decades, it would be incorrect to assert that the Pakistani state elite has not developed a sense of its own interests, even though some may disagree with the content of those interests or how those interests were developed. There is, for example, a long-standing recognition of being in a ‘tough’ geography, with insecure borders on at least three sides. There is also a persisting notion that it faces a periodically existential threat from a much more powerful eastern neighbour and that this threat should be countered by a military deterrent. This in turn can only be obtained by forging reciprocal relations with more powerful states. The presence of these interests/ ideas does not invalidate the fact that the state’s own actions and responses may have hastened insecurities in various ways. Nor can it paper over the fact that the processes through which the state recognises its context and develops its response are heavily skewed towards a largely insulated military-bureaucratic state apparatus. Both, in turn, lead to other domestic problems, including frequent civil-military political conflict and law and order insecurity in the peripheries. However, while some reduce Pakistan’s subordination to its geography or the original conditions of its creation, one can make the more substantive case that it remains in that place by the nature of the global economic order since the 1970s and due to its own economic dysfunction. With basic processes of capital accumulation stagnating or being rendered highly inefficient, the dollar requirement to ensure subsistence-level growth under global conditions of economic liberalisation can only be met through wilful subordination to varied benefactors. Periodic balance-of-payment crises since the 1980s have precipitated this pattern, and geopolitical posturing to extract IMF concessions or rents in other forms has cemented it. Each successive crisis of the last four decades has found resolution via subordination in the geopolitical domain: favour garnered with the Gulf monarchies via military assistance or labour provision in exchange for reserve deposits; providing the US with regional geopolitical support in exchange for IMF approval, or allowing Chinese capital to make infrastructure investments to kickstart (fleeting) economic growth. Ultimately, each temporary staving off of an economic crisis has pinned down the state’s subordinate position. And in the process little has been done to fix the underlying issue of domestic economic dysfunction. The writer teaches politics and sociology. X: @umairjav Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
items.description: Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over the distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected youth leaders, contrasting the expenditure with what he described as poor salaries paid to Nigerian soldiers. Utomi, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said it was troubling that an APC youth leader could display expensive vehicles at a time Nigerians had been told that government funds were limited. In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi wrote: “Nigerian soldiers are being paid peanuts as salaries, yet an APC youth leader is flaunting SUVs worth billions of naira. This is the same government that told Nigerians there was no longer money in the treasury. At this point, they must think we are fools!” In another post, the professor questioned whether the money spent on the vehicles could have been put to better use, particularly in the health sector. “Each of the SUVs in this video costs more than ₦100 million. I wonder how many world-class ambulances the millions being spent on these vehicles could buy. What a pity!” he wrote. The comments followed a video posted by APC National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, showing brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs he said were presented to selected youth leaders to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” Israel wrote. He also expressed gratitude to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “The party is supreme and that supremacy will show in our action in this election period — we will deliver polling unit by polling unit,” he added. The video, which has since been deleted, drew criticism from Nigerians on social media, with some questioning the timing of the vehicle distribution amid the economic hardship associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms. Utomi’s remarks add to the criticism surrounding the display, with the NDC chieftain raising questions about public spending priorities and the cost of the vehicles. items.title: Zone de Boulmiougou, Zongo jusqu’ et Zaktouly: Cinq (05) commerces fermés pour pratiques de prix illicites, quatre (04) réquisitionnés pour des travaux d’intérêt général
items.description: La Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) a mené une opération dans la zone de Boulmiougou, de Zongo jusqu’à Zaktouly. À l’issue de cette descente, cinq lieux de commerce ont été fermés, trois (03) boutiques de vente de produits de grande consommation et deux (02) magasins de vente de ciment. Les fermetures sont consécutives à des pratiques de prix illicites et à un défaut de publicité des tarifs. Concernant le ciment, les équipes de contrôle ont vérifié les carnets de vente et constaté que les prix appliqués dépassaient largement le tarif officiel fixé par les autorités. Parmi les cinq commerces sanctionnés, quatre (04) contrevenants ont été réquisitionnés pour exécuter des travaux d’intérêt général, conformément aux mesures disciplinaires en vigueur. La BMCRF rappelle que ces opérations s’inscrivent dans sa mission de protection des consommateurs. 80 00 11 84 / 80 00 11 85 / 80 00 11 86 BMCRF, la garantie d’une concurrence saine et loyale L’article Zone de Boulmiougou, Zongo jusqu’ et Zaktouly: Cinq (05) commerces fermés pour pratiques de prix illicites, quatre (04) réquisitionnés pour des travaux d’intérêt général est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: ‘We are not bandits’ – Herdsmen; want 30% of agric budget, 417 grazing reserves
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Pastoralist groups have rejected the profiling of Fulani pastoralists as bandits and called on President Bola Tinubu to immediately declare a national dialogue on farmer-herder conflicts, following what they say are the killings of hundreds of pastoralists in recent months. At a news conference on Sunday in Abuja, President of Kautal Pulaaku Fulbe Association of Nigeria, Dr. Huseini Buzaye, who signed an address on behalf of the Confederation of Pastoralist Non-Governmental Organisations CONPA, said the groups represent “millions of Nigerian pastoralists from all 36 states and FCT”, under over 30 associations. General Secretary of the association, Abdullahi Ardo, who read the prepared speech on behalf of the president, said; “For too long, the word ‘Fulani Pastoralist’ has been profiled and criminalized as synonymous with banditry, kidnapping and terrorism”. The groups said the stereotyping “has given impetus to jungle justice, extrajudicial killings, and hate speech against innocent pastoralists, including women and children who have no connection to crime.” “Criminals are criminals and have no tribe,” the statement said, urging security agencies and the media to “stop ethnic profiling but arrest and prosecute criminals as individuals, not as an ethnic group”, they added. On the killings, the coalition said in the last few months, hundreds of innocent pastoralists have been killed in coordinated attacks in Plateau, Niger, Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara and other parts of the country. It said women, children and the elderly were among the dead, thousands of cattle were rustled or killed, and entire Rugas were burnt down. “These killings are not reported. There is no national outrage. There is no compensation. There is no justice,” it said. The groups demanded an independent investigation into the killings. They also asked the Federal Government to direct the National Emergency Management Agency NEMA and the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons NCFRMI to provide relief materials to displaced pastoralists “as it does for other communities”. They also asked security agencies to protect pastoralists “as Nigerian citizens under Section 14 and Section 33 of the 1999 Constitution.” The coalition commended Tinubu for creating the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development, calling it “a historic decision that gave us hope after 60 years of agitation.” But it said the ministry “remains largely unfunded and without a clear operational framework” years after its creation. It appealed for the ministry “to be seen active at the community level”, and asked the President and the National Assembly to allocate at least 30 per cent of the agricultural budget to it, to “immediately gazette and protect the 417 grazing reserves”, and to start pilot ranches and fodder production in the six geo-political zones. “Livestock is a 30 trillion economy. It cannot be treated with levity,” the statement said. Citing what it described as more than 20,000 deaths from the farmer-herder conflict in 10 years, the coalition said: “Nigeria cannot achieve peace by military means alone.” It called on the President to make “a Presidential Declaration of National Dialogue and Reconciliation on Farmer-Herder and Pastoralist Conflicts”. It said the dialogue should include Miyetti Allah groups, traditional rulers, the Christian Association of Nigeria CAN, Jama’atu Nasril Islam JNI, security agencies and state governments, with a mandate of “Truth, Justice, Forgiveness, Compensation, and a Roadmap for Peaceful Co-existence.” The groups also listed responsibilities for pastoralist communities, urging leaders, households and young people to respect farmers’ rights and lawful property, take “reasonable measures to prevent livestock from entering cultivated farmland”, and cooperate with lawful security investigations. They urged them to report cattle rustling and kidnapping, and to reject violence, banditry and retaliatory violence. The coalition said it intends to carry out mass awareness and sensitisation across the six geo-political zones, with a framework already worked out. “We are Nigerians. We are pastoralists. We are not bandits. We love this country. Our cattle feed this nation,” the statement said. It called on federal and state governments, traditional institutions, farmers’ associations, security agencies and development partners to work together, advocating “justice without discrimination, security without exclusion, development without marginalization, and peaceful coexistence based on mutual respect and the rule of law.” END The post ‘We are not bandits’ – Herdsmen; want 30% of agric budget, 417 grazing reserves appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Exploit médical au CHR de Gaoua : Une masse myomateuse de plus de 4 kg retirée chez une patiente de 48 ans
items.description: Après une demi-décennie de souffrance silencieuse, une patiente de 48 ans a retrouvé la santé et le sourire au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Gaoua. Une équipe chirurgicale conduite par le gynécologue Dr Bèbè Robert Palé est parvenue à lui extraire une masse myomateuse totale impressionnante de 4,280 kg lors d'une hystérectomie de haute précision. Réalisée en environ une heure, cette intervention d'exception a permis de neutraliser la tumeur tout en préservant l'équilibre hormonal de la patiente. Cet exploit médical met en lumière l'expertise du personnel soignant de la région du Sud-Ouest et rappelle l'urgence d'un suivi gynécologique régulier pour diagnostiquer ces lésions avant qu'elles ne deviennent invalidantes. Pour cette femme de 48 ans, le quotidien s'était progressivement transformé en un pénible parcours du combattant. Depuis près de cinq ans, des myomes utérins — communément appelés fibromes — se sont développés de manière démesurée jusqu'à occuper un volume colossal dans sa cavité abdominale et pelvienne. Cette masse volumineuse entraînait des douleurs persistantes, de l'anémie, une sensation de lourdeur constante et un inconfort majeur, dégradant profondément sa qualité de vie au quotidien. Face à la gravité et à l'ampleur de la tumeur, le Dr Bèbè Robert Palé et son équipe composée d'ingénieurs en soins infirmiers et obstétricaux (spécialisés en chirurgie et anesthésie) ont déployé une stratégie opératoire de haute précision. Les praticiens ont opéré via une incision sus et sous-ombilicale pour réaliser une hystérectomie totale avec conservation des annexes. Expliquant ce choix médical, le chirurgien indique que cette méthode permet d'éliminer définitivement le foyer de développement des myomes tout en maintenant l'imprégnation hormonale naturelle de la patiente, lui évitant ainsi les désagréments d'une ménopause précoce et brutale. L'intervention, qui a duré environ une heure, s'est déroulée avec une maîtrise parfaite des risques anatomiques et hémorragiques. À l'issue de l'acte chirurgical, la pesée de la masse retirée a confirmé la mesure du calvaire enduré : 4,280 kg. C'est un véritable fardeau physique et psychologique qui s'est envolé pour cette quadragénaire, désormais en phase de convalescence et habitée par un immense soulagement. Cet acte réussi illustre la compétence, le dévouement et le savoir-faire technique du corps médical du CHR de Gaoua, capable de prendre en charge des pathologies complexes en milieu hospitalier régional. Tumeurs bénignes développées à partir du tissu musculaire de l'utérus, les myomes sont très fréquents chez les femmes en âge de procréer et lors de la périménopause. S'ils restent parfois asymptomatiques, ils peuvent engendrer de graves complications lorsqu'ils prennent du volume, telles que des compressions mécaniques des organes voisins, des douleurs intenses, des anémies sévères, voire des difficultés à mener une grossesse. À travers le succès de cette opération, les spécialistes rappellent qu'un examen gynécologique annuel associé à une échographie pelvienne constitue le moyen le plus efficace de détecter ces lésions à un stade précoce, évitant ainsi le recours à des interventions lourdes. L’article Exploit médical au CHR de Gaoua : Une masse myomateuse de plus de 4 kg retirée chez une patiente de 48 ans est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Accept results, close ranks – Asiedu Nketiah urges NDC aspirants
items.description: The National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has urged aspirants in the party’s constituency executive elections to accept the results and unite after the contest. Speaking at the Ketu North Constituency Delegates Conference at Weta in the Volta Region on Sunday, October 25, he said rebuilding unity after the elections was more important than individual victories. “What matters is not who wins, but how that person wins and how we are able to put the party together after the election,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah explained that he had deliberately stayed away from constituency elections across the country to avoid influencing delegates or appearing to favour particular candidates. He said neutrality was essential to his role as National Chairman, allowing him to reconcile members after the polls, regardless of the outcome. “Everybody in the NDC is my friend and family member. If I select some of you and call you my friends, it means the others are my enemies, but I believe all of you are my friends,” he said. He urged unsuccessful aspirants not to interpret defeat as rejection by the party. Only one person could occupy a position at a time, he noted, adding that other opportunities to serve could arise. Mr Asiedu Nketiah encouraged delegates to let the best candidates emerge and urged aspirants to accept the outcome in good faith. He expressed confidence that the elections would strengthen the NDC if members remained committed and worked together after the results were declared.

items.title: Season of protests
items.description: A WAVE of protests is sweeping across the world in a season of unrest. From West to East, the street is confronting the state. Led predominantly by students and young people, protests have been widening to encompass other disaffected groups in society. In some cases, they are morphing into a nationwide movement. On almost every continent, governments are being put on notice that there will be a price to pay for misgovernance and being indifferent to public demands. India’s Gen Z has been in the streets in anti-government protests against the controversial revision of electoral rolls. Students in France began protesting against deteriorating school conditions with other groups, including trade unions, joining demonstrations over high living costs and inequality. In Italy, students, farmers and truckers took to the streets in protests driven by education costs, economic grievances, and anti-war sentiment. In Brussels, students marched over education funding. Spain saw protests over a housing crisis. In Albania, student-led demonstrations occurred over living costs and a controversial tourism project linked to Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law. In Portugal, protests erupted over housing and falling living standards. There were education protests across Greece. In Brazil, thousands joined a student march against the election bid of far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. Tunisia’s capital witnessed protests demanding the president’s resignation and democratic rights. The triggers vary, as do the underlying causes. Each protest is rooted in its own political context. But there are common themes. All reject the status quo and indicate disenchantment with traditional political parties. All voice anger against unresponsive governments and the state failing them on their socioeconomic demands. The context for most protests is a cost-of-living crisis and deterioration or cuts in public services compounded by the state’s inability to deliver on education and jobs. Economic grievances and resentment of inequality are a driving force of the protests. A sense of disenfranchisement is another common thread. The heavy-handed response by governments to the protests and draconian crackdowns further fuelled the unrest and sparked violent clashes in several places. But it energised demonstrators to keep returning to the street. Unfortunately, in France protests degenerated into looting and rioting . Protests in Europe and India share a defining feature. They are propelled by a wave of student activism. At their core is youth frustration in a generation that sees broken promises and an uncertain future. It feels betrayed by the lack of educational and economic opportunities. Protes­ters have also been venting rage against political leaders who have ignored public needs and are seen as venal. Initiated by young people, protests have expanded into broader movements as other disaffected groups, with their own set of demands, joined the demonstrations. Social media has been a key mobilisation tool in all the protests. Governments have been put on notice that misrule and ignoring public needs will have consequences. None of the protests or movements have been party-led. Political parties have largely been sidelined, even as they tried to leverage the demonstrations; France’s left aligned itself with the protesters. In several European countries, protests are playing out in an environment of deep polarisation, which parties of both the left and right are trying to exploit. This is especially because elections are due next year in many countries including France, Spain, and Italy. In India, the youth ‘Cockroach’ movement has spearheaded the protests and mounted the most significant challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government so far. The ongoing protests came against the backdrop of student protests led by the Cockroach party over the leak of exam papers in May, which forced the resignation of the education minister. This time, the catalyst was the revision of voter lists by India’s election commission, which apparently involved the removal of around 130 million voters. The government and the election commission’s claim that this was aimed at eliminating duplicate and ineligible entries was widely rejected. It was instead seen as a step towards mass disenfranchisement. It became the trigger for youth protests , demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner and scrapping the revision. India’s opposition parties also joined the demonstrations and decried the move as a politically motivated purge to benefit the ruling BJP. The Cockroach Janta Party used the opportunity to broaden its campaign. The government’s strong-arm tactics to suppress the popular upsurge only inflamed the demonstrators who accused Modi of “stealing democracy”. While these protests did not pose an existential threat to Modi, his jittery and increasingly autocratic government behaved as if they did — with arrests and a harsh clampdown. The scale of the protests and the government’s repressive response eroded Modi’s authority, weakened his grip on power, and dented his credibility and image. The mass protests signified much more than opposition to the voter roll overhaul. They have been about democratic rights and democratic ac­­c­o­­untability and against pervasive injustice. As Indian academic Sudhir Kumar Suthar has arg­ued, they have been driven by the quest for dignity as much as for rights. The message from the young is clear: “they deserve a more dignified life than what they have received from the system so far.” The central question is what will be the outcome of mass protests and what will they achieve? A definitive assessment has to wait until the protests play themselves out as most are still unfolding. But one unintended consequence of the current wave of discontent in some European countries, especially France but to a degree also in Spain and Portugal, may be to strengthen the far-right. The far-right has led none of these protests but it stands to benefit from their fallout. In a political landscape where the political centre is being hollowed out and centrist parties have lost touch with young people, unrest advantages the most organised opposition force that promises order. In France, that force is Marine Le Pen’s Rassemblement National. Where the hard-right is in power the advantage works differently. It enables governments to cast the protests as a law-and-order issue fuelled by migrants to justify harsher measures. More generally, youth-led protests may force governments to take more seriously the needs and aspirations of young people which have rarely been a priority. What the streets are signalling is a breakdown of trust that can no longer be brushed aside. For now, the protests have put governments on notice: misrule has consequences. The writer is a former ambassador to the US, UK and UN. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.description: Dernière ligne droite avant les élections législatives en Israël. Le scrutin se déroule ce mardi 27 octobre et le pays est divisé entre les partisans de Benyamin Netanyahu et ses opposants. items.title: South Africa to allow fund managers 100% foreign assets under new framework
items.description: South African fund managers will be able to hold 100% of portfolios in foreign assets under ring-fenced mandates, regulators said on ​Friday, in a new framework that exempts qualifying vehicles from a ‌longstanding 45% offshore investment cap. The South African Reserve Bank, National Treasury and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange briefed investors on the draft Synthetic Financial Centre (SFC) framework, published on Wednesday, which would ​allow licensed asset managers, banks, insurers and private equity firms to manage ​global portfolios in any currency from a South African base. The ⁠45% limit would still apply when an institution commits capital to an SFC ​vehicle. But once the funds are inside a registered mandate, the manager could ​invest them entirely offshore. The originating institution would still count the investment towards its own prudential foreign limit. Stuart Theobald, executive chairperson of Krutham, a think tank, and convenor of Operation Phumelela, ​a private sector initiative led by the JSE to boost the competitiveness ​of South Africa’s financial sector, called the lifting of the cap “the most fundamental change” in the ‌framework. Close ⁠to 5 trillion rand ($301 billion) in South African portfolio assets are held offshore, much of it routed through overseas centres because local rules have made it difficult to manage fully global portfolios from Johannesburg. “The SFC really positions South Africa ​with a framework that ​makes it competitive,” ⁠JSE CEO Valdene Reddy said. The framework is part of a sweeping overhaul of South Africa’s decades-old exchange controls that the JSE ​estimates could attract 10 trillion rand in investment over time. Olano ​Makhubela, head ⁠of the SARB’s Financial Surveillance Department, said the 45% prudential limit would remain a “long-term feature” of South Africa’s capital-flow framework. Vukile Davidson, chief director of financial markets and ⁠stability at ​National Treasury, said a second phase could consider ​tax alignment and could allow foreign-currency listings on South African exchanges. The draft is open for ​public comment until November 30.

items.title: Health hazzard: Fruit vendors use laundry detergents to sparkle produce for profit
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan A disturbing new trend is fast gaining ground across major open-air food markets, sparking urgent public health warnings and triggering widespread panic among consumers. Read Also: Unhealthy profit: Fish vendors now using dye to fake freshness Economy&Lifestyle findings revealed that several local fruit vendors are systematically washing their produce with synthetic laundry detergents and liquid soaps. The dangerous practice is aimed at stripping away natural grime, pesticide residues, and blemishes, giving the fruits an unnaturally vibrant, polished sheen that irresistibly attracts unsuspecting buyers, while drastically cutting down on spoilage losses. From glossy, deep-green watermelons and bright yellow bananas to spotless apples, these chemically enhanced fruits have flooded urban centers. However, medical experts warn that this aesthetic transformation comes at a catastrophic cost to human health, turning nutritious snacks into toxic hazards. The glittering deception For many traders operating in highly competitive, low-margin environments, the pressure to move inventory before it rots is immense. Traditional washing with clean water often fails to remove stubborn mud or agricultural sprays, leaving produce looking dull. A vendor at a local market, speaking on the condition of anonymity, candidly explained the financial motivation behind the chemical cleansing. “Customers buy with their eyes first. If a watermelon looks dusty or faded, they will walk right past your stall to the next person. When we use a little detergent or liquid soap in the washing water, it cuts through the dirt instantl “It gives the fruits a beautiful, shiny coat that looks fresh from the farm. It helps us sell faster and reduces waste, which means more profit for us at the end of the day.” The practice is not limited to watermelons. Bananas, mangoes, and citrus fruits are also being subjected to these chemical baths. Because synthetic detergents contain powerful surfactants, they strip away the fruit’s natural protective waxy layer, replacing it with an artificial gloss that mimics premium, imported produce. On his part, Audu Musa, a fruit seller said: “The use of laundry detergent to wash fruit is to remove the dirt of mud from them and make them attractive to consumers. “But I don’t use detergents. I take my fruits to the market and shade them the way they were brought from the farm. My customers prefer them that way.” It was also discovered that when these fruits are washed with detergent, they are displayed like that without rinsing off the detergent water. This method makes the fruits appear glossy and attractive. While the vendors see an increase in patronage, food safety advocates and medical professionals are deeply alarmed. Unlike specialized, food-grade vegetable washes, household detergents are formulated with complex chemical compounds, including linear alkylbenzene sulfonate, optical brighteners, artificial fragrances, and bleaching agents. These chemicals are designed for fabrics and surfaces, not human consumption. Dr. Amara Nwosu, a gastroenterologist at a public teaching hospital, warned that the immediate and long-term health consequences of ingesting these chemical residues are severe. “Ingesting even trace amounts of laundry detergent can cause acute gastrointestinal distress, including severe abdominal cramps, vomiting, and chronic diarrhea. What is more terrifying is the long-term impact. “Consistent exposure to these industrial surfactants can severely erode the mucosal lining of the gut, disrupt the gut microbiome, and potentially lead to chronic kidney damage or liver toxicity over time. “Fruits are supposed to heal the body, not poison it.” The porous nature of certain fruit skins means that the chemicals do not just stay on the surface; they can seep directly into the flesh. Consumers who fail to peel or thoroughly scrub their fruits are effectively consuming household cleaning agents with every bite. Outrage and fear in the markets As word of the practice spreads, consumer anxiety has reached an all-time high. Many shoppers report feeling betrayed by traders they have trusted for years. Halima Yunusa, a trader, expressed her shock and deep concern over the lack of food safety ethics. “It is completely heartbreaking to realize that the things we buy to keep our children healthy could actually make them sick. “I used to think a shiny apple or a perfectly clean mango was a sign of quality. Now, I am terrified to buy anything. “How can anyone prioritize a little extra profit over human life? The government needs to step in and police these markets immediately.” As authorities scramble to contain the situation, food safety experts are advising consumers to be wary of fruits that appear excessively glossy, artificially bright, or carry a faint, unnatural floral scent. For now, the golden rule for shoppers is shifting away from aesthetic perfection toward a cautious preference for the natural, unpolished look of safe food. items.title: ‘I visit Ozzy’s grave every day’ – Sharon Osbourne
items.description: It’s been 15 months since Ozzy Osbourne died at the age of 76, at his home in Buckinghamshire. Although he had suffered from health problems for years, including Parkinson’s disease and a fractured vertebra, his death was a shock. Less than three weeks earlier, he performed on stage in Birmingham for a triumphant farewell concert. After the show, he was on a high. “He was just so, so happy,” his wife Sharon recalls. “He was online, going through the reviews and saying, ‘There’s something terribly wrong’, and I’m like, ‘Why?’ “He goes, ‘I didn’t get slagged by anybody. Why are people being nice to me?’ “And I’m like, ‘Because they like you’.” On the morning he died, Ozzy woke up early and went downstairs for his usual morning workout. Shortly afterwards, he had a heart attack. An air ambulance was called, and paramedics tried to save him. But it was too late. “I was asleep,” says Sharon. “We’d spoken in the night. Ozzy had woken in the night, and he asked me to kiss him twice, and I did. “And then he said, ‘Hold me, hold me tight,’ and I did. “And then the next thing I know, it’s early in the morning, and someone comes rushing into the room saying, ‘Come down now’. “I ran down, and that was it.” Sharon and Ozzy Osbourne, pictured in 2017 after renewing their wedding vows The grief, she says, will never leave. “You’ve lost the love of your life, so you don’t just wake up and go, ‘I’m fine now. I’m cured’. “You never get over it. But you learn to live with it, and that’s what I’m trying to do. So you either sit in a room and don’t come out, or you accept it, befriend it, and that’s it.” The affection among Ozzy’s fans was apparent before the singer’s funeral. Thousands of people lined the streets of Birmingham, laying floral tributes and singing Black Sabbath songs as Ozzy’s body was transported through his home city in a hearse topped by a purple floral tribute in the shape of a cross. Sharon says he would have been mystified by the outpouring of love. “He’d have been like, ‘What’s the matter with you guys? Go home!'” she says. But for the family, the public response was a huge source of comfort. Daughter Kelly said last year: “I never could have imagined it to be as helpful as it has been to know that we’re not alone in our grief and our sadness, and that the rest of the world loved him as much as we did.” Sharon says the fans’ cards and messages were all collected, sorted and photographed; while the flowers were composted for the family garden, where Ozzy is buried. “There was no way I could put Ozzy in a public graveyard,” she says. “I’ve seen what happens to other people in the public eye. There’s no peace because people want to come and they want to pay their respects. That’s an ongoing thing, and I wanted Ozzy to rest and just be.” Does she visit him often? “Of course, every day. I can see him from my window.” She still talks to him regularly, she says. Asked what she discusses, she puts a finger to her lips and gives a gentle “shh”. Ozzy’s family – including children Jack and Kelly – stopped to read the tributes during his funeral procession last July Ozzy and Sharon’s relationship spanned more than 50 years. They met in 1970 and married in 1982. Their time together could be turbulent – he was arrested for attempting to murder her in 1989 (she dropped the charges), and they split briefly in 2016 amid rumours of infidelity – but the couple maintained that they were soulmates. “It was an unusual relationship because we had such highs and such terrible lows,” she admits. But at the end of his life, “he knew” how much he was loved. You can see proof of that love – from his family, his fans and his bandmates – in a new documentary about his final gig at Birmingham’s Villa Park last year, when he reunited with heavy rock legends Black Sabbath. Titled Back To The Beginning, it features more than 25 songs from that star-studded concert, including Ozzy’s solo set and Sabbath’s full performance. In backstage footage, fellow A-list performers discuss the star’s influence in awestruck tones. “If there was no Sabbath, there’s no Metallica,” says the band’s frontman James Hetfield. “It’s as simple as that.” Yungblud, whose version of Changes was one of the concert’s emotional high points, says that, as a kid who didn’t fit in, Ozzy changed his life. “The fact he was celebrated for his madness and his individuality gave me hope.” Sharon says the concert was Ozzy’s final wish: the one thing that would make him happy after years of deteriorating health. But it almost never happened. Six months before the show, Ozzy fell and fractured his vertebrae. In recovery, he caught pneumonia three times. After surgery on his back, he caught sepsis and nearly died. Two weeks before the show, doctors urged him to call it off. “They came to see us at the house and they said, ‘You can’t do this. We’re advising you not to do this. Your heart’s too weak’,” Sharon recalls. But the singer was determined to see it through. In the film, it’s hard to believe he’s so ill. Although he performs seated on a throne, his eyes are full of life and his voice is powerful. As he looks out at the crowd, he seems elated. Backstage, Sharon admits, “the whole family was terrified”. But something changed when Ozzy entered the stadium. “He was sat in his dressing room, watching everybody on a screen performing, and he was like, ‘I just can’t believe they’re all here’. “It’s amazing what support and love and determination can do for you, because [before the show] he was somebody that couldn’t breathe. He had a lung condition. He had a heart condition. He had terrible, terrible agony from his spine. He had blood clots and he had Parkinson’s. “Some days just to even talk was an effort, let alone sing. And I don’t know how he did it, but he did it. “And you saw it in his eyes, in his face. It just made him feel like he was alive again.” Ozzy is survived by Sharon, their three children (left-right: Kelly, Aimee and Jack) and three children from his previous marriage The effect was so galvanising that, when he came off stage, Ozzy declared he wanted to go on tour. “He was raring to go,” Sharon laughs. “He was like, ‘I can do this, and the fans don’t mind if I’m sat down’.” It’s an incredible and rare thing, I suggest, to be able to grant your partner their last wish. Ozzy may have suffered immense pain in his final years, but he was able to say goodbye in style. “To quote one of his songs, he was flying high again,” Sharon says. “He was just floating for those last 17 days. It was great. It was joyous.”

items.title: Wheat price dilemma
items.description: THE announcement of an indicative wheat price of Rs4,500 per 40 kilograms may have come too late for Sindh farmers, but it is welcome as far as it goes. That is not far. The figure is Rs1,000 higher than last year’s and, by the government’s account, reflects rising production and fuel costs. It is also Rs500 short of what farmers demanded. And there is no word on who will buy the grain or when. An indicative price is a signal, not a guarantee. Since April 2025, when the government dropped the support price and suspended large-scale procurement, farmers have been promised a market-based system that would serve them better. It has not. The crop now being sown is the third to go into the ground without a floor. Punjab’s experience this April shows what happens when a procurement price is announced without a mechanism to enforce it. The province tried to revive buying through bank-backed private aggregators. The banks doubted the scheme’s viability, and the aggregators bought only 160,000 tonnes against a target of 2.5m tonnes. Prices fell anyway. A price no buyer is obliged or financially equipped to pay is only a number. Growers seem to have grasped this before the government did. Consumers, meanwhile, are not being spared. Over five years the price of wheat has gone up by 150pc, and that rise goes straight to the price of flour. Punjab has used the price as its only tool instead of working on the cost of farm inputs, which the federal government’s policies have kept high. Flour in cities is selling for Rs160-190 per kilogram, which is hard on poor households. Even the government’s stocks are expensive. Sindh began selling government wheat this month at Rs12,500 per 100kg, or Rs5,000 per 40kg. That is more than the prime minister has offered farmers. The test of wheat reform is not whether the government can step out of the market. It is whether the system that replaces government buying shares the risk fairly among farmers, traders, millers, banks, and the state, keeps flour affordable, and protects the country’s food supply. For now, farmers carry most of the risk while everyone else looks after their own interests. With sowing already underway, the government should say in plain terms what it will buy, through which agency, with what money, and by when. It should adapt its imports to that plan. It should look at the cost of fertiliser and other inputs, instead of relying on price alone. And it should help poor households directly, instead of keeping flour cheap for all by squeezing the grower. A price announcement with no buyer behind it will not persuade anyone to sow, and a market that works for only one side is not worth defending. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: IPoB alleges secret transfer of 68 detainees
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Indigenous People of Biafra, IPoB, has alleged that 68 detained Biafrans were secretly transferred from Wawa Barracks to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja, accusing the Federal Government of using the justice system to prolong the detention of its members. The group also alleged that the Court of Appeal had yet to list an appeal challenging the conviction of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, despite the compilation and transmission of the record of appeal. IPOB made the allegations in its weekly address issued on Sunday by the Head of its Directorate of State, DOS, Mazi Chris Nwaogu. Nwaogu said the group’s legal team had identified the 68 detainees and was working to secure their release. He urged supporters to sustain legal efforts on behalf of those in custody. He further alleged that a separate fundamental rights suit concerning Kanu’s detention had suffered a setback after the presiding judge reportedly announced that the court file was missing. According to him, the suit concerns Kanu’s detention for 14 months following his discharge by the Court of Appeal on October 13, 2022. The IPOB spokesman also challenged the legal basis of Kanu’s conviction by Justice Omotosho on November 20, 2025, alleging that the judgment relied on a repealed law. He cited Section 36(12) of the Constitution, which provides that a person cannot be convicted of a criminal offence unless the offence and its penalty are prescribed in written law. Meanwhile, IPOB disowned an audio message circulating online that purportedly announced the return of an enforced Monday sit-at-home across the South-East. Nwaọgụ said neither the DOS nor the High Command of the Eastern Security Network, ESN, had authorised the action, warning against attempts to enforce an unauthorised shutdown. He urged residents to disregard the message and avoid actions capable of provoking violence or disrupting economic activities in the region. The group also announced what it described as a phased political disengagement, directing its supporters to boycott activities associated with the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It urged supporters to stay away from APC rallies, stop carrying the party’s flags and refrain from defending APC governors, while maintaining its position on boycotting the 2027 elections. Nwaọgụ said the proposed boycott was a response to what the group described as injustice, unlawful detention and persecution of its members. He, however, cautioned supporters against violence and warned politicians against hijacking the planned boycott for their own interests. IPOB reiterated its demand for Kanu’s immediate and unconditional release, urging the judiciary to list the appeal for hearing and determine the legal issues surrounding his conviction. items.title: Boromo : 43 motos, 33 tricycles et 130 sacs de minerais confisqués lors d’un raid antiorpaillage
items.description: Selon les informations rapportées par l'Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB), une opération conjointe d'envergure menée les 18 et 19 octobre 2026 par les agents forestiers et la Compagnie républicaine de sécurité (CRS) de Boromo a permis de démanteler un site d'orpaillage clandestin au cœur de la forêt classée des Deux Balé. L'intervention s'est soldée par la saisie d'un important matériel roulant et d'équipement d'extraction, comprenant notamment 43 motos, 33 tricycles, 130 sacs de minerais et plusieurs groupes électrogènes. Alors que les activités illégales se poursuivaient malgré de nombreuses actions de sensibilisation, cette fermeté affichée par les services forestiers et les forces de sécurité vise à garantir la protection de cette aire protégée et la préservation durable des ressources naturelles. D'après une dépêche de l'Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB), la forêt classée des Deux Balé a été le théâtre d'une offensive ciblée contre l'exploitation illégale des ressources minières. Les 18 et 19 octobre 2026, les agents des Eaux et Forêts et les éléments de la Compagnie républicaine de sécurité (CRS) de Boromo ont uni leurs forces pour mener une opération conjointe au sein de cette zone protégée. L'objectif affiché était de mettre un terme définitif aux activités d'orpaillage clandestin qui s'y sont développées en violation de la réglementation environnementale. L'intervention des forces de l'ordre a permis de porter un coup d'arrêt sévère à la chaîne logistique des orpailleurs illégaux. Sur le terrain, un important lot de matériel servant à la recherche, à l'extraction et au transport du minerai d'or a été saisi. Le bilan comptabilisé par les autorités fait état de 43 motos, 33 tricycles, 130 sacs de minerais, 137 poulies, 26 bouteilles de gaz et 16 piqueurs. À ces équipements spécialisés s'ajoutent des groupes électrogènes, six sacs de riz ainsi que divers vivres récupérés sur place par les équipes d'intervention. Cette opération d'envergure s'inscrit dans le cadre du renforcement de la lutte contre l'exploitation aurifère clandestine au sein des aires protégées du pays. Comme le souligne l'AIB, les orpailleurs continuaient de mener leurs activités prohibées au cœur du massif forestier, en dépit des multiples campagnes de sensibilisation menées antérieurement par les services compétents. À travers ce déploiement de force et la confiscation des moyens d'exploitation, les services forestiers et la police entendent réaffirmer la primauté de la loi, protéger la biodiversité de la forêt des Deux Balé et préserver les ressources naturelles nationales. items.title: Kojo Kwarteng: From journalism and corporate communications to law
items.description: On Friday, October 9, 2026, Emmanuel Kojo Kwarteng became a lawyer, adding the legal profession to a diverse career spanning journalism, marketing, corporate communications, public relations, banking, authorship, alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and community service. His story shows the power of continuous learning. He has never regarded education as an end, but as a tool for professional excellence, personal transformation and service to society. From Dunkwa-on-Offin/Tarkwa to Professional Excellence Kwarteng began at Boa-Amponsem Primary School in Dunkwa-on-Offin and Tarkwa Senior High School, where he served as Library Prefect, an early sign of his interest in knowledge, leadership, and service. He studied at the Ghana Institute of Journalism and the University of Ghana Business School, earned a Bachelor of Science in Administration, and later an MBA in Marketing from Central University. He then earned an LLB and LLM from Mountcrest University, Ghana and the University of Essex in the United Kingdom, and studied at the Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, Evanston, Illinois, USA. He has also undertaken executive master’s-level studies in Labour and Industrial Relations Law and Practice and ADR. This breadth lets him see organisations through the connected lenses of business, law, communication, marketing and dispute resolution. A Journalist Who Understands the Power of Information As an award-winning journalist at Ghana News Agency and Daily Graphic, Kwarteng covered public affairs, politics, business and society, gaining an appreciation of credible information and the media’s role in holding institutions accountable. As a Presidential Reporter, he covered the Presidency and national affairs, gaining a front-row understanding of governance and public policy. He is also credited with founding the Federation of Environmental Journalists (FEJ) in Ghana in the mid-1990s, which launched the war against illegal mining, environmental destruction, and abuse of communities’ rights. Corporate Communications, Public Relations and Marketing A defining chapter was his time as Head of Corporate Affairs at GCB Bank Plc, where he worked at the intersection of corporate leadership, media relations, stakeholder engagement, and reputation management. In his philosophy, corporate communication goes beyond press releases. It means building trust between an organisation and its stakeholders, managing reputation, communicating in a crisis, and ensuring employees, customers, regulators, shareholders, the media, and the public understand decisions. He is regarded as one of the best in his generation, and during GCB’s 2017 integration of UT/Capital Bank and the 2023 Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP), he was a household name in financial services. His marketing training complements this, shaping his view that an organisation must not only provide value, but also communicate and protect it. Why the Law Is a Natural Progression His entry into law is a natural extension of his career, not a departure. His interest in ADR fits this background. Disputes are inevitable, and what matters is whether they become destructive or are managed constructively. ADR offers solutions without prolonged litigation, reflecting his commitment to dialogue, negotiation and peaceful resolution. Author and Thinker Kwarteng has written two books. Leading an Extraordinary Life explores personal development and the belief that people can improve themselves through discipline, knowledge and purposeful action. Oil Cocoa Mines is a novel that shows his creative side. He has also written and reviewed many articles on business, leadership, communications, law and society. Environmentalism, CSR and Philanthropy He is committed to environmental advocacy, corporate social responsibility and philanthropy, believing organisations and professionals have responsibilities beyond profit and personal advancement. He has developed policy documents for national and international institutions and NGOs. For him, success carries a responsibility to contribute to society. A Man of Faith and Service A committed Christian, Kwarteng worships at Assemblies of God Church, Christ Worship Centre, Sowutuom, Accra, where he serves as a deacon and chairs the Education and Welfare Committees. This reflects leadership as service without seeking the spotlight, and a belief that spiritual development and human wellbeing complement each other. A Multidisciplinary Professional What stands out is not the number of qualifications but how they intersect across law, business, journalism, communications, marketing, banking, labour relations, ADR, social responsibility, environmental advocacy, authorship and Christian service. In a complex world, professionals who connect disciplines are increasingly valuable. A corporate crisis can be a legal, financial, communication, reputational and human resource problem at once, and his career has prepared him to see those connections. Another Chapter Begins October 9, 2026, marks not the end of his journey but the start of another chapter. From TARSCO to the legal profession, his path demonstrates lifelong learning and shows that career development need not be linear. The common thread is not a job title but the continuous pursuit of knowledge and the desire to use it meaningfully. The greater achievement lies in bringing his qualifications together to solve problems, mentor others, strengthen organisations and serve society.
