items.title: ‘No shake-up in PTI committee structure’
items.description: • Spox rejects reports about core committee being ‘sidelined’ • ‘Strengthening’ of parliamentary body suggested, but not decided, says Panjutha ISLAMABAD: Amid a deluge of reports suggesting a change in the party’s decision-making structure, the PTI on Sunday rejected the notion that its core committee had been ‘sidelined’, or its powers re-designated to another body. Sheikh Waqas Akram, the party’s central information secretary, said the core committee, the political com­mittee and the parliamentary party were separate forums, each with their own, distinct responsibilities. Organisational and political decisions fell within the remit of the core and political committees, while the parliamentary party dealt with legislative and parliamentary issues. He said the parliamentary party’s recommendations were given due consideration and could be referred to the relevant committees, adding that final authority over all decisions rested with PTI founder Imran Khan, who had delegated powers to the committees. PTI leader Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that during a meeting, Bar­rister Ali Zafar had suggested stren­gthening the parliamentary committee, but it was just a recommendation and no such decision was made. “Imran Khan had entrusted the political committee with the authority to make decisions, while directing that the core committee should also be… taken into confidence before decisions were finalised. The core committee had a large membership, which made decision-making difficult. That was one of the reasons for forming the political committee — to facilitate decisions and reduce the chances of discussions being leaked,” he said. He said that there was also a proposal to include heads of the party’s organisational bodies in the political committee. “Subsequently, the mandate for the movement and negotiations was given to Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas, while Sohail Afridi was entrusted with the authority to lead the street movement. How can any change be made without Imran Khan’s approval?” he questioned. Furthermore, the PTI also rejected a statement attributed to PTI interim chief Barrister Gohar Ali Khan suggesting that the KP chief minister could have avoided detention by staying in Mardan but he travelled to Peshawar as part of a “pre-planned master plan”. Imran, Bushra’s ‘ordeal’ Meanwhile, in a separate statement, the party condemned the prolonged detention of its founder and his wife, the denial of their fundamental and constitutional rights, and the use of state machinery to intimidate political opponents. The party warned that continued disregard for constitutional safeguards, due process and the sanctity of private homes was setting an alarming precedent that could threaten rights and freedoms of all citizens. In a statement, Mr Akram claimed that Imran Khan had spent 1,177 days in detention at Adiala Jail, including 356 days in solitary confinement, while Bushra Bibi had remained behind bars for more than 911 days. He said that the prolonged detention of both, restrictions on their meetings with family members, lawyers and party leaders, and growing concerns about Mr Khan’s health and medical care required immediate attention. He demanded that Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi be granted all their legal, fundamental and constitutionally guaranteed rights, including regular meetings with family members, lawyers and the party leadership. He called for appropriate medical care under the supervision of Imran Khan’s personal physician and a comprehensive examination by qualified medical specialists. He also condemned the continued detention of Imran Khan’s sisters, despite the completion of their reported 30-day detention under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) law. He demanded their immediate release, along with that of detained PTI leaders, elected representatives and party workers, adding that preventive detention must not become an instrument for punishing political dissent or silencing opposition voices. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Russia, US, Ukraine signal plans for trilateral talks in November
items.description: US President Donald Trump said Sunday that trilateral talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine will take place "very soon," signaling renewed diplomatic efforts to address the conflict, while Moscow and Kyiv have outlined their positions on the proposed negotiations. Trump did not provide a specific date for the meeting, but said he believed both Russia and Ukraine were interested in reaching an agreement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy subsequently confirmed that the three countries were planning technical-level working talks in November. The venue remains under discussion, with Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates, other locations in the Middle East and European cities among the options. Zelenskyy said the working-level discussions were meant to pave the way for a subsequent higher-level meeting, including talks among the three countries' leaders. Initial discussions are expected to focus on a ceasefire involving energy infrastructure and areas related to the Black Sea. Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushako said Sunday that Moscow was prepared to resume trilateral negotiations after November 4. He cautioned, however, that the talks would constitute an initial contact and that expectations should not be too high, adding that further efforts would be needed to reach a peace agreement. Ushakov also said dialogue with European countries would be necessary to resolve the Ukraine conflict. Kyiv sets out negotiating red lines While expressing readiness to engage in further talks, Zelenskyy stressed that Ukraine must determine its own security arrangements and that Kyiv would not accept conditions unilaterally imposed by Russia. In a Sunday interview, he said limiting the size and capabilities of Ukraine's armed forces and requiring the country to remain neutral were not on Kyiv's negotiating agenda. Territorial issues, he added, should be discussed exclusively at the leaders' level. Zelenskyy said Washington had repeatedly raised the idea of a "territorial exchange" and proposed other possible approaches, but Ukraine would not accept an arrangement involving the exchange of territory for other concessions. He said technical working groups could address other issues, while territorial questions should be reserved for direct negotiations among the leaders. These topics could form part of the discussions planned for November. Zelenskyy also opposed lifting all sanctions against Russia before a meeting among the US, Russian and Ukrainian leaders. He said sanctions relief should follow an appropriate process and sequence if the goal was to end the conflict. Kyiv had communicated its position to US representatives, he said, stressing that Ukraine should not give up important negotiating leverage, including sanctions, related funds and frozen assets, before a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Humanitarian ceasefire and unresolved military needs Alongside the diplomatic preparations, Zelenskyy said a temporary ceasefire in the Russian-controlled southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky had been proposed by the United States starting on Tuesday to facilitate humanitarian operations. He said the pause in fighting would last several days because humanitarian assistance and civilian evacuations could not be completed in a single day. Under the proposed arrangement, personnel from the United States, Ukraine and Russia would participate in the humanitarian effort. Russia would clear landmines from roads, while Ukraine would verify the clearance work and take part in subsequent humanitarian operations. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian authorities had coordinated the preparations with relevant security agencies and the military. However, Kyiv's military needs remain a point of concern in its dealings with Washington. Zelenskyy said three issues had been raised during US-Ukraine talks in Oslo: shortages of air defense systems, restrictions affecting Starlink and Starshield services, and limits on US intelligence sharing with Ukraine. He said the latter two issues had been resolved, but air defense supplies remained unresolved. Although deliveries of US Patriot air defense missiles had made some progress, Zelenskyy said the pace was too slow to meet Ukraine's urgent needs. Commitments alone were insufficient, he argued, if deliveries were delayed by one or two months.

items.title: ‘Replace complexity with compassion’ – Cardinal Turkson urges students
items.description: The Chancellor of the Catholic University of Ghana, Cardinal Peter Appiah Turkson, has urged students to embrace compassion and collective responsibility as they prepare for a world shaped by conflict, technological disruption and uncertainty. He said university education must go beyond academic achievement to instil ethical values and prepare graduates to contribute meaningfully to society. Cardinal Turkson was speaking at the university’s 25th Congregation and 38th Matriculation Ceremony at Fiapre, near Sunyani, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. The university admitted about 1,810 students and graduated 2,806, comprising 668 postgraduate and 2,138 undergraduate students. It also celebrated its first PhD graduate, Dr Godfred Etse Klugah. Drawing on the concept of a volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous world, commonly described as VUCA, Cardinal Turkson proposed a more human response to its challenges. He encouraged students to replace volatility with vulnerability, uncertainty with unlearning, complexity with compassion, and ambiguity with answerability. “The religious twist gives an ethical content to everything that seeks to transform the volatility, the uncertainty, the complexity and the ambiguity into something more human and more ethical,” he said. He explained that recognising vulnerability should encourage people to seek and offer support rather than face life’s challenges alone. “We are vulnerable, and because we’re vulnerable, we need to support each other with the common wisdom that we develop and acquire here,” he told the gathering. Cardinal Turkson also urged students to remain open to learning by letting go of prejudices and habits that could hinder their development. “To progress and to move on in life, we need to unlearn a lot of things. We need to let go of a lot of traits that we’ve come here with, and we need to forget and abandon lifestyles and prejudices with which we’ve come here,” he said. He said compassion should guide academic and social relationships, fostering collaboration and mutual support. Turning to artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, he cautioned against reducing human beings to figures and numbers at the expense of their inherent dignity. He cited conflicts in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan, alongside rapid technological and economic changes, as examples of the difficult environment young people must navigate. On answerability, Cardinal Turkson said students must be willing to account for their choices. “In providing answers for everything that we do, we show responsibility, we show maturity,” he said. He described university education as building on lessons and values acquired at home, in school and across society. Like a manual for a new product, education should guide people in navigating life. He congratulated the graduates and encouraged newly admitted students to make the most of their university experience. The Bono Regional Minister, Joseph Addae Akwaboa, called on the university to strengthen practical learning, digital skills and industry partnerships to prepare students for the changing job market. He said education and youth empowerment remained central to Ghana’s long-term development. “The No Fee Stress Initiative is an important intervention aimed at easing the financial burden on eligible first-year students in public tertiary institutions,” he stated. Mr Akwaboa also urged the university to use research and innovation to address youth unemployment, agricultural productivity, sanitation and public health challenges. He assured the institution of the Bono Regional Coordinating Council’s commitment to partnerships that support regional development.

items.title: Foreign participation in capital market strengthens considerably in half-year 2026
items.description: Foreign investor participation in the capital markets strengthened considerably in the first half of 2026, according to the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report. This supported a decline in the risk of capital flight. The improvement was on the back of the issuance of the new bonds amidst improved macroeconomic conditions and financial market prospects. According to the report, improved macroeconomic conditions, declining sovereign risk perceptions, and continued exchange rate stability contributed to maintaining investor confidence and reducing the risk of sudden capital outflows. Overall, foreign investor participation is expected to remain robust if current macroeconomic stability is sustained. Sovereign Risk Spreads Meanwhile, Ghana’s sovereign risk spreads have been relatively stable since the last Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting and compared favourably with peer economies in the sub-Saharan Africa region. The stability reflects improved investor sentiment, and this is expected to have a positive knock-on effect on the country’s risk ratings while supporting inflows of portfolio investment and foreign direct investment.

items.title: Parliament’s Finance Committee has had no reason to worry over government bills – Adongo
items.description: Parliament’s Finance Committee Chairman, Isaac Adongo, says the committee has had no reason to worry about government bills brought before it, citing bipartisan scrutiny and broad agreement among members. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition, he said the chairman does not dictate the committee’s decisions. “The good thing is that we have not had any reason to be worried. The reason is that almost every bill that has come to us has been scrutinised on a bipartisan basis.” His comments followed a question about whether he could confront his good friend, Finance Minister Dr Ato Forson and reject proposals that went beyond what Parliament had approved. Mr Adongo said scrutiny depended on the whole committee. He pointed to the experience of opposition members, including Ranking Member and former Finance Minister Dr Amin Adam, Deputy Ranking Member Dr Stephen Amoah, and Dr Gideon Boako. “So it is not about the chairman of the Finance Committee. It is the work of that committee taking into account the interests of the nation, and very often all those that have come to us, we have not had reason to disagree as a committee.” He said disagreements gave members on both sides an opportunity to express their views, although the committee largely agreed on proposals. Mr Adongo cited the bill that established the Gold Board as an example. He said opposition members had concerns about some provisions but did not oppose its underlying principle. “The passage of the bill that led to the establishment of the Gold Board, for instance, from a political perspective, our colleagues do not disagree in principle, but their side of the divide was not comfortable with certain provisions.” He defended the decision to pass the legislation and credited the Gold Board with what he described as a monumental impact. But he acknowledged that shortcomings could emerge and require changes. “Of course, over time, there will be some lapses that can be identified, and a review is possible at any point in time.” Isaac Adongo said he believed opposition members would support a review if the executive returned to Parliament seeking changes to particular clauses.

Attacks continued over the ‌weekend ⁠with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on ​Sunday ​it had ⁠intercepted more missiles and drones. The top oil exporter restarted partial ​operations at its main airport ​on ⁠Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks, even as ⁠the ​militant group vowed to ​keep targeting the facility.

items.title: Brazil: Lula Should Focus on Human Rights in New Term
items.description: Click to expand Image President-elect Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva voting in the second round of the 2022 presidential election, São Bernardo do Campo, Brazil. © 2022 Rovena Rosa/Agência Brasil (São Paulo, October 25, 2026) – Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who has been reelected as Brazil’s president, should use his new term to tackle chronic human rights problems, Human Rights Watch said today. President Lula defeated the Liberal Party candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, in a runoff election on October 25, 2026, official results from the Superior Electoral Court show. Lula received 51.7 percent of the vote, while Bolsonaro received 48.2 percent, with 99.9 percent of the ballots counted, according to the Superior Electoral Court. “During his current term, President Lula has supported democratic institutions and made important progress on protecting forest and local communities who depend on it for their survival, but had a mixed record in other areas,” said César Muñoz, Brazil director at Human Rights Watch. “His administration should address the record high numbers of killings by the police and other public security problems, and more consistently support human rights policies at home and abroad.” News media reported reduced public transportation services in several states, which may have barred voters from reaching voting stations on October 25. Federal police were reportedly investigating possible electoral crimes. The Lula campaign asked for an extension in the voting time in some states due to those disruptions. The Bolsonaro campaign also asked for an extension in other areas of the country due to rain. As the polls were closing, a Supreme Court justice extended the voting time for two hours. Shortly after, the Electoral Court, and later the Supreme Court justice, established that the extension applied to voting stations that were still open. After taking office in January 2023, President Lula took important steps to repair some of the damage that the previous administration had inflicted on democratic institutions, the environment, and human rights protections overall. Yet, chronic human rights problems continued to plague the country, including abuse by the police, which disproportionately affects Black Brazilians. Killings by police reached a record high—with 6,589 people killed in 2025—and had kept rising in 2026 as of September, driven by failed public policy strategies that have allowed the unchecked use of lethal force by police. Abusive police practices undermine public security—a primary concern for Brazilians, according to many polls—by feeding mistrust and making communities less willing to collaborate with police, while fueling a cycle of violence that endangers both civilians and police officers. They also create an environment of impunity for excessive use of force in which police corruption and involvement with organized crime flourish. While public security is primarily the responsibility of states in Brazil, the federal government has a crucial role to play in coordinating and promoting public security policies that are more effective at dismantling criminal organizations, protecting the public from violence, and upholding human rights. An important measure to improve investigations that President Lula should support is to remove forensic services from police, to ensure independent analysis in police abuse cases and other crimes. During an interview on October 15, President Lula defended trying and punishing as adults 16- and 17-year-old children accused of certain serious crimes. The measure would violate international law, which says that children should be subject to justice systems that are distinct from those for adults. That proposal would also undermine rather than strengthen the country’s efforts to reduce crime, Human Rights Watch said. Children who break the law can and should be held accountable, but in an individualized manner that promotes their rehabilitation. On the environment, President Lula should reverse inconsistencies that endanger the rights of Brazilians. His administration brought Amazon deforestation to the lowest level on record, according to official data, and resumed demarcating Indigenous territories. Yet, it took insufficient steps to regulate the cattle industry, historically the largest driver of deforestation and its related human rights abuses. His administration also initiated a long-awaited national program to reduce the use of pesticides. However, the administration continued to allow the use of highly hazardous pesticides, many of which are banned for use in the European Union and elsewhere because of proven harm to health and the environment. This puts Brazilians at risk of acute poisoning and other serious health impacts, particularly Indigenous, Afro-descendant, and small farmers’ communities. Major corruption scandals involving a range of politicians, political parties, and institutions have unfolded in recent years. The Lula administration should promote measures to strengthen the fight against corruption, including working with Congress to ensure transparency and oversight over budget allocations. Other long-standing human rights problems that President Lula should prioritize include gender-based violence, severe obstacles to abortion access, violence against human rights and environmental defenders, and the institutionalization of people with disabilities due to lack of sufficient community-based support services. Some incidents marred the electoral campaign. Non-profit organizations compiled 134 cases of threats and violence against candidates and politicians from various parties, in the first 50 days of electoral campaign. Brazilian media also reported that Meta, which operates Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, restricted some content and features that promoted Lula’s candidacy in the lead up to the election. Meta said it had experienced technical issues but contended that it did not favor one candidate over another. Brazil’s electoral court ordered Meta to take measures to ensure equal treatment of the candidates. Meta’s Oversight Board—an external body that can overturn Meta’s moderation decisions and provides non-binding policy guidance—expressed concern about recurrent failures in the company’s “election integrity efforts,” citing the “breakdown” that harmed Lula’s campaign. “President Lula, who cannot run for office again in 2030, has a chance to leave a mark on the country by seeking solutions to long-standing problems that make a real difference in protecting rights and liberties for all Brazilians,” Muñoz said.

items.title: Senegal party that controls parliament comes out against revised budget bill
items.description: Senegal’s Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government’s ​revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country ‌can push ahead with its debt restructuring, A statement by the party headed by former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko cited “disagreements over certain budgetary decisions, the chosen ​financing arrangements and the insufficient guarantees provided to parliament”, though ​it said the party was open to engaging with ⁠the government on getting a new budget in place The West ​African nation has been grappling with a debt burden that had ​reached 132% of gross domestic product by the end of 2024, International Monetary Fund figures show, after the government uncovered billions of dollars in misreported borrowing ​by the previous administration The government reached a staff-level agreement, with the IMF ​in early September for a $2.2 billion, 36-month Extended Credit Facility to support its ‌reform ⁠program. But without parliamentary approval of the revised budget, the government risks delaying the IMF program, which underpins its entire debt restructuring strategy, Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo plans to hold a press ​conference on Sunday ​to discuss the ⁠revised budget “which is intended to implement a revised framework aimed at improving the quality of life ​of Senegalese people” The amended 2026 budget bill paints ​a sharply ⁠deteriorating fiscal picture. It cuts real GDP growth to 2.7% from roughly 5% in the original budget and widens the deficit to ⁠7.6% ​of GDP from 5.4%, driven largely by ​a tripling of energy subsidies to 790.3 billion CFA francs ($1.36 billion) from 250 billion

Lula logra una remontada histórica en Brasil y da la victoria a la izquierda frente al avance ultra de los Bolsonaro
items.description: Lula escribe un nuevo capítulo épico en una trayectoria legendaria. El izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , de 80 años, presidente de Brasil y uno de los políticos más influyentes de América Latina en este siglo, ha conseguido la ansiada remontada este domingo. Lula ha derrotado al senador Flávio Bolsonaro, de 45 años, heredero político del clan ultraderechista , con el 51,7% de los votos frente a los 48,2%, es decir, cuatro millones de votos más. Es el primer mandatario que vence tras perder la primera vuelta en una elección en el gigante latinoamericano. Solo el emperador Pedro II y Getúlio Vargas han gobernado por más tiempo. El líder del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT) conquista un cuarto mandato, para los pies a la extrema derecha y confirma su fortaleza, pese al odio que genera en buena parte de sus compatriotas. Lula, que el martes cumple 81 años, gobernará un Brasil profundamente dividido y se consolida como resistencia del progresismo ante Donald Trump. Seguir leyendo

items.title: RD Congo: quand les chemins de l’opposition commencent par Rome!
items.description: Pourquoi l’opposition congolaise ne s’est-elle pas encore prononcée sur ce retour dans le maquis de Joseph Kabila, qui a pris la tête, le 12 octobre 2026, du mouvement politico-militaire du Front pour la refondation nationale (FRN), dans le but de reconquérir le pouvoir par les armes? Quelle sera la position d’ensemble des opposants sur le dialogue national prévu par le président Félix Tshisekedi, un dialogue qui est dit inclusif, mais laisse à quai certains opposants? Que pensent ces mêmes opposants du charcutage de la constitution que s’apprête à opérer le chef de l’Etat congolais avec pour finalité de s’offrir un troisième mandat présidentiel? Autant d’interrogations qui trouveront, peut-être, réponse sur les chemins européens de l’opposition battant pavillon C64 et dont la tournée sur le vieux continent commence, ce lundi, par Rome, en Italie. Alors que la RDC subit la furie dévastatrice de Ebola Bundibugyo qui continue d’y faire des ravages malgré le dispositif de lutte, et de traverser allègrement les frontières, se promenant désormais entre l’Afrique centrale, l’Afrique de l’Est et l’Afrique de l’ouest, les politiciens congolais eux, se déchirent autour du pouvoir. Un pouvoir que le président Félix Tshisekedi compte conserver après ses deux mandats constitutionnels et que ses opposants entendent lui arracher au nom de la sacro-sainte règle de l’alternance démocratique. Visiblement maître du jeu, du moins pour l’instant, et pour gagner du temps, le chef de l’Etat congolais prépare, sereinement, son dialogue national dit inclusif, mais qui a largué certains opposants. Parmi ces derniers, l’homme le plus ciblé n’est autre que l’ancien président congolais, Joseph Kabila, condamné à mort par contumace, en septembre 2025, par la justice de son pays. Il n’a jamais aimé le Congo, a dit Félix Tshisekedi, évoquant la nouvelle option de Joseph Kabila de prendre les armes contre son pays, à travers une rébellion armée. En effet, le prédécesseur du président congolais avait déjà, sur le dos le grief de collusion avec les combattants de l’AFC-M23 que le Rwanda est accusé de soutenir, d’où sa condamnation à mort. Mais sa sortie du bois révèle, désormais, sa détermination d’en découdre ouvertement avec Kinshasa, pour faire partir son successeur dont il a pourtant favorisé, à l’époque, la victoire à des élections contestées qu’il a organisées en décembre 2018. Question: Joseph Kabila a-t-il choisi la bonne option alors que l’opposition luttait contre sa mise à l’écart du dialogue national qualifié d’inclusif, mais en réalité exclusif, de Félix Tshisekedi? Si c’est, indubitablement, le moyen pour l’ancien président congolais de se replacer dans un jeu politique totalement verrouillé par son successeur, il n’en demeure pas moins qu’il aura, difficilement, l’aval d’une opposition républicaine pour qui le pouvoir ne peut être conquis que par les urnes, dans une république démocratique. Sur quel soutien compte donc Joseph Kabila pour assouvir son dessein belliqueux, alors que des défections de cadre sont déjà observées dans son camp? Du reste, avant même la tournée européenne du C64, l’opposant Augustin Matata Ponyo Mapon, ni plus ni moins, ancien Premier ministre de Joseph Kabila, a, peut-être, esquissé la position de l’ensemble de l’opposition, en affirmant sa conviction que le pouvoir, en RDC, ne peut se conquérir par les armes. C’est dans cette même dynamique que Félix Tshisekedi, pour contrer l’offensive guerrière de Joseph Kabila, a sonné la mobilisation de sa majorité parlementaire. En tout cas, c’est loin d’être le fait du hasard si la tournée des opposants congolais, commence par Rome, siège de l’Eglise catholique, très influente sur la politique en RDC. Par Wakat Séra L’article RD Congo: quand les chemins de l’opposition commencent par Rome! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: F1: Antonelli (Mercedes) remporte le GP des Etats-Unis et se rapproche du titre
items.description: Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) a remporté dimanche à Austin le Grand Prix des Etats-Unis de Formule 1, 18e manche sur 23 de la saison, mais devra attendre au moins une semaine pour être sacré champion du monde. L'Italien, qui a décroché sa neuvième victoire de la saison, a devancé le Monégasque Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) et le Néerlandais Max Verstappen (Red Bull). Antonelli est passé tout près de s'adjuger sa première couronne planétaire puisqu'il n'aura besoin d'inscrire que deux points dimanche prochain à Mexico pour être titré. « C'était le résultat dont nous avions besoin. Toute l'équipe le méritait vraiment car on travaille très dur. L'exécution a été parfaite et la stratégie à un seul arrêt était la bonne. On est très proche (du titre) et on va essayer de finir sur une bonne note et le décrocher rapidement », a souligné l'Italien. Parti en pole position, Antonelli a parfaitement réussi son départ pour garder les commandes de la course au premier virage, avant de s'échapper. L'Italien, qui a appliqué une stratégie à un seul changement de pneus, n'a pas tremblé pour s'imposer devant Leclerc et Verstappen, qui, eux, se sont arrêtés deux fois. Le septuple champion du monde anglais Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) a pris la quatrième place, devant son compatriote Lando Norris (McLaren), qui était deuxième jusqu'à dix tours de la fin mais a reculé face à des adversaires équipés de pneus plus frais. Le Français Isack Hadjar (Red Bull), qui s'était élancé en troisième position, a eu du mal au démarrage et a ensuite été victime d'un problème moteur, ce qui l'a fait reculer à la sixième place. L'Australien Oscar Piastri (McLaren) a terminé septième, après avoir résisté brillamment face au Britannique George Russell (Mercedes), une nouvelle fois décevant. La lutte pour la deuxième place au championnat s'annonce très serrée puisque Russell, Hamilton, Verstappen et Leclerc se tiennent seulement en neuf points. Le Top 10 est complété par le Néo-Zélandais Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) et le Français Pierre Gasly (Alpine), qui retrouve la zone des points avec quatre courses de disette. Le troisième Français, Esteban Ocon (Haas), a, comme souvent, pris un très bon départ, passant de la 15e à la 12e position, avant de finalement achever la course au 14e rang. The post F1: Antonelli (Mercedes) remporte le GP des Etats-Unis et se rapproche du titre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Spotify uploads lyrics for Dolly Parton’s Welsh version of Jolene in Irish
items.description: Spotify mistakenly uploaded the lyrics to Dolly Parton’s Welsh version of her hit Jolene in Irish. The song was recorded before her death on 25 August and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis and Parton’s niece, Jada Star. The version has parts sung in English and Welsh, but the lyrics on the digital audio streaming service Spotify showed the language as Irish. Spotify removed the Irish lyrics after the BBC approached it for comment. The BBC asked Spotify when it uploaded the single and lyrics, when it noticed the error, and when it would be replaced, but it did not respond. The lyrics on Spotify have been removed since the BBC approached the service for comment The single came out on 9 October , and is the second posthumous release from Parton – who was of Welsh descent. The legendary country artist won 10 Grammy Awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote more than 3,000 songs over a seven-decade career. Jolene was released in 1973 and is about the fear she might lose her husband, Carl Dean, to a red-headed bank clerk who had flirted with him early on in their marriage . It was was nominated for a Grammy in 1974, gave Parton her second number one single on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart and her first foray into the main Hot 100 chart (60). It has since earned more than one billion streams on Spotify, and many famous singers have covered Jolene. Lewis and Star recorded their parts in the UK, while Parton recorded her parts in her studio in Nashville The Welsh version came about after Lewis, from Neath, translated the country classic and posted it on social media. Then Star, Parton’s niece, reached out and suggested recording Jolene in Welsh with Lewis – and Parton joined too. In 2008, during a concert at the Cardiff International Arena, Parton reportedly revealed her Welsh ancestry to fans in the crowd. The star revealed that one side of the family, from Parton’s mother, Avie Lee Owens, was initially believed to be from Conwy. Following the singer’s death, research by staff at Conwy Council’s archives suggested Parton’s ancestors were from Machynlleth, in Powys, not Conwy as previously thought.

items.title: Fitch revises Access, Zenith, UBA, GT, 5 others outlook to positive
items.description: Fitch Ratings has revised the Outlooks of nine Nigerian banks and two bank holding companies to Positive from Stable. Their Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) have been affirmed at ‘B’. The affected issuers are Access Bank Plc, Zenith Bank Plc, First HoldCo Plc (FHC), First Bank of Nigeria Ltd (FBN), United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), Guaranty Trust Bank Limited (GTB), Fidelity Bank PLC, First City Monument Bank Limited (FCMB), Wema Bank PLC and Bank of Industry Limited (BOI). According to the UK-based firm, the Outlook revisions to Positive follow a similar action on Nigeria’s ‘B’ Long-Term IDRs on 9 October 2026 that reflects ongoing reform of the policy framework and Fitch’s increased confidence that momentum will not be disrupted by upcoming elections. The revision of the Outlooks on the Long-Term IDRs of Access Bank, Zenith Bank, FHC, FBN, UBA, GTCO, GTB, Fidelity Bank, FCMB and Wema Bank reflects Fitch’s view that the sovereign’s credit profile and Nigeria’s operating environment may become less of a constraint on the issuers’ standalone creditworthiness. The revision of the Outlook on the Long-Term IDRs of FHC and FBN is supported by the issuers having restored compliance with the total capital adequacy ratio (CAR) requirement. BOI’s Outlook revision reflects our view that the government’s ability to provide support to the policy bank may improve. The National Ratings of all the issuers and the Government Support Ratings (GSRs) of the eight commercial banks and two bank holding companies are unaffected.

items.title: Brésil : Lula réélu pour un quatrième mandat
items.description: Le président de gauche est arrivé en tête du deuxième tour de l’élection présidentielle du Brésil, après une journée marquée par de nombreuses perturbations un peu partout dans le pays. Le président brésilien Lula est arrivé en tête du deuxième tour de l’élection présidentielle . Il a devancé son adversaire de droite Jair Bolsonaro d’un peu plus de quatre millions de voix (51,8 % contre 48,2 %). Avec 45 % des voix contre 47 % pour son concurrent, Lula avait pourtant été devancé au premier tour par le fils aîné de l’ancien président d’extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro (2019-2022), condamné pour tentative de coup d’État. Quelque 160 millions d’électeurs ont été appelés aux urnes pour décider si le pays devait rester l’un des derniers bastions de gauche en Amérique latine, ou rejoindre la vague de droite dans la région, encouragée par le président américain Donald Trump. Les dernières heures avant le dépouillement ont été marquées par une grande confusion. À quelques minutes de l’heure initialement prévue pour la fermeture des bureaux de vote, un juge de la Cour suprême a décidé de la prolonger de deux heures. La plus haute juridiction du pays a été saisie par l’équipe de campagne de Lula, qui a dénoncé le fait que des bus aient été retirés de la circulation dans des villes comme Sao Paulo (sud-est), dirigée par un maire de droite, ou Salvador de Bahia (nord-est). Mais le temps que l’ordre soit transmis à chaque bureau, certaines urnes électroniques avaient déjà été fermées et le dépouillement avait débuté. Le juge Zanin, nommé par Lula à la Cour suprême, a dû préciser ultérieurement que la prolongation du vote ne s’appliquait que pour les urnes qui n’avaient pas été fermées au moment de sa décision. Vidéo Blanchiment d’argent, lien avec des criminels : l’héritier Bolsonaro aux portes du pouvoir Le camp Bolsonaro avait lui aussi réclamé au TSE la prolongation du vote dans deux États, le Minas Gerais (sud-est) et le Rio Grande do Sul (sud), en raison de fortes pluies dans ces régions. L’extension des horaires « n’est que justice, chacun doit avoir le droit de voter et cela a été négligé », dit à l’AFP Jacqueline Maria Lima de França. Cette entrepreneuse de 34 ans suit le dépouillement sur un écran géant avec d’autres partisans de gauche dans le centre de Rio. Autre son de cloche parmi des partisans de droite à Brasilia. « C’est une honte », s’indigne Aurelio Junior, dentiste de 45 ans. « Ils ont inventé cette prolongation de deux heures pour tenter d’équilibrer le résultat », assure-t-il. Afp avec Le Parisien L’article Brésil : Lula réélu pour un quatrième mandat est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Riyadh airport reopens as Houthis, coalition exchange attacks
items.description: King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh partially reopened on Sunday as Yemen's Houthi group and the Saudi-led coalition continued to exchange attacks, and the Houthis warned airlines and travelers against using the airport. The airport had suspended operations following a series of Houthi attacks that caused multiple deaths and injuries. On Sunday, the Houthi group said it had launched dozens of ballistic missiles in three attacks against the kingdom, the first of which targeted King Khalid International Airport and "successfully achieved its objective." Other attacks targeted King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait and a Saudi Border Guard naval base in Jazan. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea renewed a warning to airlines, employees and travelers against using King Khalid International Airport, describing it as "unsafe." He also issued a broader warning against using Saudi airspace while excluding the airspace over Mecca and Medina. Separately, the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency quoted a military source as warning workers and civilians "not to approach Saudi oil facilities," while cautioning Saudi Aramco shareholders of "losses" if they continued to hold shares in the company. The Saudi-led coalition on Sunday said it had intercepted and destroyed a total of 12 missiles and two drones launched toward the kingdom, including a ballistic missile and two drones targeting the Riyadh region. The Saudi General Directorate of Civil Defense said a Saudi citizen and an Asian resident were injured when debris from two intercepted ballistic missiles fell in Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah governorates, while three residential buildings and seven vehicles were damaged. The Houthi group said Sunday's attacks came in response to what it described as "Saudi aggression" on Sanaa and other Houthi-held areas a day earlier that left "dozens of people killed or wounded, including women and children." Earlier Sunday, Sarea said Saudi forces had carried out 56 air and missile strikes over the past 24 hours, targeting what he described as "civilian sites" in the provinces of Hajjah, Lahj, Amran, Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Ibb. A local security official told Xinhua News Agency that loud explosions were heard later on Sunday in Yemen's southern port city of Aden, concentrated around the Salah al-Din area of Al-Buraiqa district, a strategically important area that hosts key military bases of government forces and the Saudi-led coalition. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage, nor were there comments from the Houthi group. The latest exchanges come amid a sharp escalation between the Houthi group and Yemeni government forces backed by the Saudi-led coalition, with intensified ground fighting accompanied by Saudi-led airstrikes on Houthi-held areas and Houthi missile and drone attacks on government-held territory. Also on Sunday, Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy said during a meeting with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres in Cairo that the league rejected attacks on Arab countries and reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its right to defend its security and sovereignty. Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of northern Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition intervened in the conflict in 2015 in support of the internationally recognized Yemeni government.

items.title: Sharp rise in prices of smartphones burdens consumers
items.description: • Average cost of mobile phone with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage has risen to around Rs40,000 compared to Rs22,000 a few months ago • Dealers say while govt taxes have not increased significantly, rising cost of chips is affecting rates of new handsets • Market survey shows lower, middle-income groups hit hardest • Consumers say abrupt price hike hampers connectivity in digital age KARACHI: A sharp rise in mobile phone prices in the city has made new smartphones almost unaffordable for a large number of consumers as all major mobile phone brands have increased prices by Rs15,000 to Rs30,000 per handset. The increase has hit particularly hard those who could previously afford “budget smartphones”. The budget smartphone can be described as a device with bare minimum features needed to function reliably for daily essentials, such as 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage. While it used to cost around Rs20,000 until last year, it is now priced above Rs30,000, and, therefore, has gone out of reach for many. Consumers wonder why the prices have gone up so much. Some think it is because of the taxes imposed by the government while others say it is so because of the US-Iran war that has affected international trade and, with that, export of mobile phone components. For a vast majority, education, work, online transport services, banking, government services and communication with family members are linked to smartphones and, therefore, having a reliable phone is essential. Due to a steep hike in prices, a large number of buyers have no option but to buy used phones available on the market or kit phones, which are refurbished sets imported in bulk without retail packaging to avoid heavy customs duties. However, many believe that used or kit phones do not offer the same reliability which a new smartphone does. Shopkeepers said the unprecedented increase in mobile phone prices had not only made life more difficult for consumers, but had also severely affected their businesses. One shopkeeper said: “When a phone costing Rs20,000 rises to Rs30,000 or Rs35,000, many consumers can no longer afford it. Our sales have fallen drastically following the increase in prices.” Another shopkeeper said the market was currently facing uncertainty because of continued price fluctuations and a shortage of supply. The ‘reason’ behind price hike The Karachi Electronics Dealers Association president, Muhammad Rizwan Irfan, said that there had been no significant increase in taxes to affect the price so much. He said mobile phone prices had increased mainly due to the rising cost of chips. Similarly, Mian Abdul Rehman of the Pakistan Mobile Phone Manufacturers Association told Dawn that mobile phones were becoming increasingly expensive mainly because of the rising cost of RAM (random access memory) and ROM (read-only memory). He said demand for memory components had increased significantly with the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, including its use in AI systems and robotics and data centres. However, their production had not increased at the same pace as consumption. “AI companies are buying RAM and ROM at very high prices, which is driving up their cost,” he said. Mr Rehman said memory device prices had remained relatively stable before the rapid expansion of AI, but the situation had changed with the growing demand from AI-related industries. He said mobile phone manufacturers were finding it increasingly difficult to absorb the higher cost of memory components. “That’s why there has been such a significant increase in mobile phone prices,” he added. Consumers seek govt intervention Perturbed by the jacked-up prices, consumers Dawn spoke to are calling on the government to take measures to keep smartphones with basic specifications within the reach of ordinary citizens, arguing that access to digital services should not become limited to those who can afford increasingly expensive handsets. They said mobile phones are an essential part of everyday life rather than merely a means of communication or entertainment. A customer at Sareena Mobile Market in Buffer Zone said phones are a basic necessity in everyday life. “On the one hand, the government talks about a ‘Digital Pakistan’, but on the other, the price of the very device through which ordinary citizens access essential government and other digital services continues to rise,” he said, adding: “The government should take measures to keep the prices of basic smartphones affordable, so that people can access essential government apps and other digital services.” Another customer suggested that the government enter into an agreement with a mobile phone manufacturer to make basic smartphones available to consumers at affordable prices. A man, who had come to Saddar Mobile Market to buy a new phone for his daughter, who just started college, told Dawn that he realised after visiting the market that buying a new smartphone was out of his budget. “When I came to buy the phone in August, I found that the price of the model I wanted had risen from Rs22,000-Rs23,000 to around Rs30,000. When I asked the shopkeeper about the increase, he told me that there might be problems with imports, which had pushed up the mobile phone prices. “With my salary and the current inflation, I could not afford an additional Rs7,000 to Rs8,000 all at once, so I decided to wait until the following month and save some more money. But the price has increased further this month. Now I have only two options: either buy a used smartphone or a keypad mobile phone, because a new smartphone is now beyond my means,” he said. A woman at the same market said rising phone prices had forced her to spend money from her savings to buy a new smartphone. “It is my compulsion to purchase a mobile phone at an inflated price as I am a working woman and need a phone in good condition,” she said. Speaking to Dawn at North Karachi’s Abdullah Mobile Market near UP Mor, a young man said: “My mobile phone was snatched last night near KDA Chowrangi. I have come to the market to buy a phone, but even for Rs25,000-Rs30,000, I cannot find a decent handset on which essential everyday apps can run properly.” He said: “Previously, a reasonably good phone with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage could be bought for Rs20,000-Rs22,000, but shopkeepers are now quoting Rs35,000-Rs40,000 for phones with similar specifications. Under these circumstances, I may now have to settle for a lower-quality handset, start using a keypad phone that can only make calls and send SMS messages, or buy a used phone.” Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan’s food supply fails own dietary guidelines: FAO
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s food supply remains sharply misaligned with national dietary guidelines, with major shortages of vegetables, fruits, roots and tubers, and pulses, while cereals and sugar remain in excess of dietary requirements, according to a Food and Agricul­ture Organisation (FAO) policy brief. FAO’s new policy brief, “Food Supply for Healthy Diets in Pakistan,” says ensuring equitable access to diverse, nutritious, safe and affordable foods is a policy imperative, particularly as more than 60 per cent of Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet. The situation contributes to high rates of malnutrition, while diet-related noncommunicable diseases are rising alongside persistent unde­rnutrition, the report says. Pakistan adopted its food-based dietary guidelines in 2018, setting out evidence-based recommendations for the types and quantities of foods needed for healthy diets. But efforts to promote healthy eating cannot succeed unless nutritious foods are available and accessible, the brief says. The assessment compared Pakistan’s annual food supply with population-level requirements across 10 dietary guideline food groups from 2010 to 2023, identifying surpluses and gaps. Population growth is adding pressure. Pakistan’s population increased from 189.3 million in 2010 to 235.2m in 2023 and is projected to reach about 330m by 2050. Climate change and other challenges are expected to intensify demands on the agrifood system. The report identifies persistent shortages in several nutritious food groups, particularly vegetables, roots and tubers, fruits, and legumes and pulses. The estimated vegetable supply gap widened from 10.9m to 17.8m tonnes in 2010 to 13m to 21.6 m tonnes in 2023. For fruits, the gap increased from 1.9m to 10.3m tonnes to 3.9m to 14.3m tonnes over the same period. However, milk, milk products, meat and eggs showed improvement. Fats and oils moved from a small gap in 2010 into the estimated required range in subsequent years. To address the imbalance, FAO recommends coordinated fiscal and regulatory measures to realign agricultural production and trade priorities, improve food distribution, reduce post-harvest losses and food waste, and strengthen demand for healthy foods. The brief calls for updating Pakistan’s dietary guidelines to reflect nutrition, health and environmental priorities, along with nutrition education and behaviour-change efforts. It recommends evidence-based taxes on beverages and foods high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats, and front-of-package nutrition labelling to help consumers make informed choices. It urges greater agricultural investment in vegetables, fruits, pulses, roots and tubers, with support for milk production in some regions. Other recommendations incl­ude incentives for food processors to meet quality standards and reduce salt, sugar and unhealthy fats. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan, Qatar explore new avenues for trade, investment cooperation
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Qatar have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic ties, exploring new avenues for trade and investment, and expanding cooperation across key sectors, including agriculture, food security, manufacturing, information technology, maritime transport and infrastructure. The commitment was expressed during the second meeting of the Pakistan-Qatar Joint Task Force (JTF) on Trade and Investment, co-chaired by Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs Dr Ahmad bin Mohammed Al-Sayed in Doha. The meeting reviewed progress in bilateral economic cooperation since the inaugural session in April 2026 and explored practical measures to enhance trade, facilitate investment and develop industrial partnerships between the two countries. According to a press release issued here on Sunday, representatives of relevant Pakistani ministries participated virtually, while the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), which serves as the secretariat of the Joint Task Force, coordinated the proceedings from Pakistan. Doha’s investment sought in modern agriculture, grain storage facilities and advanced farming technologies GCC Free Trade Agreement During the discussions, Pakistan emphasised the importance of an early signing of the Pakistan-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Free Trade Agreement, seeking Qatar’s continued support in completing the remaining formalities. The Pakistani side informed the meeting that it had completed its domestic approval process and forwarded the approved agreement text to the GCC Secretariat on Dec 31, 2025. The proposed agreement is expected to provide a framework for strengthening trade relations and expanding market access between Pakistan and GCC member states. Pakistan also raised the issue of restrictions on its bone-in meat exports to Qatar and called for an early resolution. It highlighted that a comprehensive technical dossier addressing animal health and food safety requirements had already been shared with the relevant Qatari authorities. Agriculture and food security featured prominently on the agenda, with Pakistan highlighting a proposed MoU between the Trading Corporation of Pakistan and Qatar’s Hassad Food for rice supply. The proposal has been submitted to the federal cabinet for approval. Pakistan invited Qatari investors to explore opportunities in modern agriculture, grain storage facilities, silos, cold storage, integrated cold-chain infrastructure and advanced farming technologies. Both sides also discussed sustainable food supply arrangements. Besides, the Pakistani delegation presented investment opportunities in the automobile sector, particularly electric vehicles under the country’s new EV policy framework. Joint manufacturing, technology transfer and industrial partnerships were identified as areas offering scope for closer collaboration. Pakistan also invited Qatari investment in IT and digital infrastructure, shipping and maritime transport. The proposed Karachi-Hyderabad Motorway was offered as a potential investment opportunity for Qatar. The Qatari side stressed the importance of enhanced cooperation in civil aviation and air traffic. Pakistan welcomed the proposal and said aviation-related matters would also be taken up by the Technical Working Group on Logistics and Communications. Investment Fund Pakistan further presented the concept of an Investment Fund, highlighting opportunities for Qatari participation in infrastructure, agriculture, industrial development, information technology and other priority sectors. To translate the discussions into practical outcomes, Pakistan called for the early operationalisation of 11 Technical Working Groups identified during the first Joint Task Force meeting. These groups cover logistics, aviation, advanced manufacturing, mining and minerals, agriculture, tourism, financial technology, healthcare, education, industrial development, information technology and startups. Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to sustained engagement and effective follow-up through the Joint Task Force framework. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Israel to close all West Bank crossings on election day
items.description: • Netanyahu faces tight race against Bennett, Lapid, Eisenkot in tomorrow’s polls • Warns Iran against attempts to disrupt elections • Israeli strikes kill seven people in Gaza, including three at university HEBRON: With just one day to go before Israel’s Oct 27 general election, Israel said Sunday that all land crossings with the West Bank would be closed on election day, as an Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people, according to staff and a local hospital, while the civil defence agency reported four more deaths elsewhere in the territory. The announcement came a day after Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron and displaced around 2,000 residents, with Defence Minister Israel Katz saying, “they will not be allowed to return... until we’ve finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron.” Hamas, while not claiming credit, hailed Friday’s killings at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to exact a heavy price for the attack just days before polls and said he was planning an operation on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967. He said that Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday’s Israeli elections, warning the Islamic republic against any hostile acts. Israel’s longest serving prime minister Netanyahu is facing a tight race for a new term in Tuesday’s polls, with his security-first reputation all but shattered by the Oct 7, 2023 attack. With just one day to go before general election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a tough contest as several prominent rivals seek to end his long hold on power. Among his main challengers are former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, veteran politician Avigdor Lieberman, Arab party leader Mansour Abbas and Yair Golan. The election is shaping up to be a crucial test of Netanyahu’s leadership, with the opposition seeking to challenge his governing coalition. The Israeli army said that from Sunday, Palestinians would “not be permitted to enter Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley for work”, using terms many in Israel use to refer to the West Bank. The army also said it would enforce “a ban on the entry and exit of Pale­stinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings throughout Election Day” on Oct 27, it added. The Palestinian Authority called for international pressure on Israel to protect residents affected by the military operation. The Israeli army said that over Friday and Saturday, it operated in 40 areas throughout the territory, with locals reporting that soldiers announced evacuations over loudspeakers late at night. Israeli forces said they “apprehended approximately 40 suspects”. Right-wing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he personally ordered “the immediate demolition of a row of illegal structures” following Friday’s shooting. “Anyone who messes with us will quickly understand that he will pay a painful price,” he wrote on X. Strike on university Meanwhile, an Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory. Gaza civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal said four other people were also killed, two in an airstrike in the southern city of Khan Yunis, one in central Deir al Balah and one in the north of the Strip. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: Govt moves to establish new ‘umbrella’ privatisation entity
items.description: • Proposed legislation aims to merge Public-Private Partnership Authority and Privatisation Commission • Seeks to provide immunity to incumbent, former chairmen, secretaries and other officials ISLAMABAD: The government has introduced a bill in the National Assembly, for the establishment of a Privatisation and Public-Private Part­nership Commission (PPPPC), by merging the existing Public-Private Partnership Authority (P3A) and Privatisation Commission, to prevent duplication of institutional functions and processes. The proposed law that seeks amendments to both legal instruments — the Privatisation Commission Ordinance 2000 and Public Private Partnership Authority Act 2017 — also provides legal and investigation immunity to the current and all former chairmen, secretaries, board members, officials and consultants from any act of omission or commission in good faith and in personal capacity and commits public funds to contest any such cases. The all-powerful commission will be led by the incumbent chairman Muhammad Ali and will comprise a majority of members from the private sector, including two women directors. It will collectively administer four public funds — privatisation fund, public contributory fund, viability gap fund and PPP project development funds — created through allocation in the federal budget, receipts from international lenders, income from investments or any other source. The government claims that the PC Ordinance dealt with privatisation of SOEs under the government policy while P3A Act governed a separate body. Both frameworks were concerned with mobilising private sector capital and expertise in relation to public assets, infrastructure and services and their administration through two separate institutions entailed duplication of institutional functions and processes. Therefore, the government’s pol­icy decision was needed for establishing a single institutional framework and mechanism for carrying out privatisation and public private partnership transactions in an efficient manner. For this, it seeks to reconstitute the Privatisation Commission as the Privatisation and Public-Private Partnership Commission, to repeal the Public Private Partnership Authority Act 2017 and dissolve the P3A. The bill provides for the reconstitution of the board with a majority of independent members, including members with public private partnership experience and at least two women, fixed terms of office and clear grounds for disqualification and removal. The bill also empowers the proposed reconstituted commission to conduct functions of advising on, appraising, structuring, facilitating and monitoring public private partnership projects and the establishment of the viability gap fund, the PPP project development facility, and the public contribution fund. The draft claims that it provides a comprehensive legal framework for public private partnerships, including the contractual framework for PPP agreements, a federal PPP pipeline, the approval process, the risk management unit and PPP transaction execution committees. It also empowers the commission to set up PPP nodes within government agencies, settlement of disputes and an alternative process for below-threshold projects. The proposed law enables the commission to utilise public contribution fund to meet any government obligations with respect to PPP projects, including land acquisition, site handover, right of way and any such other enabling actions as may be required in connection with the project. All these funds would be non-lapsable. The PPP agreement between the public and private parties shall be a public document and any interested person shall be entitled to obtain its copy subject to applicable laws, and the government or the commission or the government agency shall not be held liable for any claim of the private party for a risk which is not specified in the PPP agreement. All existing contracts signed by P3A would stand transferred to the new commission without any disadvantage to the private parties. The proposed law empowers the commission to require in writing from any government agency to submit a complete list of its existing, proposed and planned projects, including projects under consideration or development, whether or not identified as PPP projects within fifteen days. The agencies shall be obligated to comply with such a requirement with full accuracy and completeness. Where a government agency fails to comply with any such requirement, the PC chairman may refer the matter to the ministry or division concerned for compliance. There will be a committee to review potential PPP projects proposed for inclusion in the federal PPP pipeline and shall provide its recommendations, which shall be placed before the board for consideration and decision. All officers, consultants, advisers, auditors, employees and other staff of the P3A shall upon the dissolution of the P3A be retained by the commission for a period of six months or until the expiration of their respective contracts, whichever is earlier, on terms and conditions not less favourable than those applicable to them immediately before the dissolution. Published in Dawn, October 26th, 2026

items.title: El Clásico: Kylian Mbappe scores twice to end Laliga leaders’ winning start
items.description: Kylian Mbappe scored twice, including an 87th-minute winner, to earn victory for Real Madrid against Barcelona in El Clasico. Barcelona were aiming to set an outright record for the most consecutive victories at the start of a Spanish top-flight season. However, Hansi Flick’s side were unable to surpass the mark of nine straight wins set by the Real Madrid team of 1968-69. Mbappe’s first goal four minutes before half-time was a fortuitous one; home defender Gerard Martin’s attempted clearance of Yan Diomande’s low cross flew in off the France striker past Joan Garcia. Both teams had created chances beforehand but the game really opened up in the period between Mbappe’s opener and the interval, with Mbappe hitting the post and Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal side-footing wide from close range at the other end. A Barcelona equaliser arrived 16 minutes into the second half as captain Raphinha collected Pedri’s pass and shot through the legs of Jude Bellingham into the far corner. Martin almost made amends for his part in Real’s goal shortly afterwards but his header was superbly clawed away one-handed by Andriy Lunin – who was starting in place of first-choice goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois with the Belgium international ruled out because of illness. When it seemed as though the points would be shared, some brilliant skill by Bellingham started a move on halfway, substitute Eduardo Camavinga broke forward and squared the ball for Mbappe to finish into an unguarded net. Visiting manager Jose Mourinho celebrated with a small knee slide by the dugout and a fist pump. League leaders Barcelona have a two-point lead over second-placed Atletico Madrid after 10 matches, with Real one point further back in third spot.

items.description: Demand for treasury bills increased as the government exceeded its target by about 12%. The government received total bids of GH¢4.26 billion from the investors, but accepted GH¢3.9 billion. A little over GH¢2.8 billion of the bids were tendered for the 91-day bill, representing 67% of the total bids. The uptake was, however, GH¢2.5 billion. The 182-day bill received bids of about GH¢533.28 million. About GH¢ 420 million was accepted. For the 364-day bill, about GH¢873 million of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢420 million of the bids were accepted. Meanwhile, interest rates went down on the shorter end of the yield curve, but rose on the longer end of the yield curve. The yield on the 91-day bill declined by a basis point to 4.61%. Again, the 182-day bill also fell to 6.27% from the previous week’s 6.31%. items.title: Gold Board concerns did not justify holding up law – Adongo
items.description: Parliament’s Finance Committee Chairman, Isaac Adongo, has defended the passage of the law establishing the Gold Board, saying concerns about some provisions did not warrant delaying it. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition, he said the minority supported the bill in principle. Its reservations concerned specific provisions. “The passage of the bill that led to the establishment of the gold board, for instance, from a political perspective, our colleagues do not disagree in principle, but their side of the divide were not comfortable with certain provisions.” Mr Adongo argued that Parliament needed to allow the institution to begin its work. He pointed to what he described as its impact as justification for that decision. “Nevertheless, we needed to get that act out of the way, and you have seen the monumental impact of the gold board, so we needed to first get a handle on it.” He said passing the law did not close the door to changes. Any weaknesses identified during implementation could be addressed through a review. “Of course, over time, there will be some lapses that can be identified, and a review is possible at any point in time.” Mr Adongo also expressed confidence that minority members would support amendments if the executive returned to Parliament with proposals to revise certain clauses. His defence came amid questions about whether he could challenge government proposals despite his party being in power. He said the committee’s decisions went beyond the chairman and reflected scrutiny from both sides. “The reason is that almost every bill that has come to us has been scrutinised on a bipartisan basis.” He cited the presence of ranking member and former Finance Minister Dr Amin Adam, deputy ranking member Dr Stephen Amoah, and Dr Gideon Boako. Mr Adongo maintained that disagreements did not necessarily signal opposition to an entire proposal. They also allowed members to put their concerns on record. “Those disagreements are basically giving an opportunity to members on both sides to air their views about what ought to be done, but largely we agree on most of the things.”

items.title: ‘Consummate actor has left the stage’ – Kanayo, others mourn Francis Duru
items.description: Nollywood actors have mourned the death of their colleague, Francis Duru, describing him as a talented performer whose contributions to the film industry will be remembered. Duru died on Friday at the age of 57 after a brief illness. His death comes two years after he lost his 15-year-old son, Ifeanyi, leaving fans and colleagues in the film industry in mourning. Actor Kanayo O. Kanayo, in a tribute on his Instagram page, described Duru as a complete actor and one of Nigeria’s most versatile and prolific performers. “A consummate actor has left the stage. One of Nigeria’s most flexible, prolific performers. Rest in peace, my brother,” Kanayo wrote. Actress Kate Henshaw also mourned Duru, reflecting on life’s brevity and praying for his soul’s repose. “Like a flame gone out, so are our lives when it all ends,” she wrote, praying for God to grant him eternal rest and comfort his family. Actress Mercy Johnson-Okojie said she was too overwhelmed by the loss to find words. “Too tired and speechless about this loss,” she wrote. Actress Stephanie Linus described Duru’s death as tragic and heartbreaking, praying for strength for his family. “Such a tragic and heartbreaking loss. May God grant his family the strength and fortitude to bear this loss. May his soul rest in peace. RIP Francis Duru,” she wrote. Duru became popular for his role as Ahanna in Amaka Igwe’s classic film Rattlesnake and built a career spanning more than three decades in Nollywood. His family announced his death in a statement on his official Instagram page in the early hours of October 23, 2026.

items.title: Brazil’s Lula clinches victory over Flavio Bolsonaro to win fourth term
items.description: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round. The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied all projections to win an unprecedented fourth term at the helm of Latin America’s largest country. According to official results, he won 51.75 percentof the votes to 48.25 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who had entered election day confident with his lead in the polls. With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. After a campaign marred by scandal and mud-slinging, Sunday’s vote plunged into chaos after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extending voting by two hours, at the request of Lula who said buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Supporters of Brazil’s President and Workers’ Party (PT) re-election candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva react to the presidential runoff election results in the state of Sao Paulo, Brazil, on October 25, 2026. Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on October 25, 2026, as he clinched election victory against right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who trounced him in the first round. (Photo by NELSON ALMEIDA / AFP) Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some parts of the country due to heavy rains, but his camp lashed out at the country-wide extension. “Either we win. Or we win. Consider yourself warned,” pro-Bolsonaro lawmaker Nikolas Ferreira wrote on X as the votes streamed in. The bitter campaign laid bare the deep divisions in the country of over 200 million people. “It’s a disgrace. We’ve never had anything like this in Brazil, and now they’ve come up with the idea of extending the election period by two hours,” said Aurelio Junior, 45, a dentist in Brasilia. Jacqueline Maria Lima de Franca, 34, a business owner in Rio de Janeiro backing Lula said it was “more than fair…everyone should have the right to vote, and that was being neglected.” – Lula rises from the ashes, again – Lula, a defining figure in Brazilian politics over four decades, was blindsided after his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro. The left swung into action with massive rallies declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro,” where protesters recalled the former president’s chaotic handling of the Covid pandemic, devastation of the Amazon rainforest and cuts to public programs. Lula also revamped his social media strategy, taking video selfies and even bought his first cellphone, while supporters carried out a feverish campaign to change the minds of family, friends and neighbors, and encourage them to vote after high levels of abstention. His re-election marks another remarkable comeback for the man who grew up dirt poor in the northeast in a family of illiterate farmers. Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months. The charges, annulled on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him. In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but voters complain about the cost of living and a sense of insecurity. Lula’s social policies became a point of tension as he expanded welfare programs during the campaign. “Brazil needs more time with Lula, primarily because the country is on the verge of falling into the clutches of fascism,” Maria Fernanda Elisbao, a 21-year-old editorial assistant, told AFP. – A tricky term ahead – Lula heads into a fourth term with a country divided, with almost half of the nation voting against him and desperate for change. “We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro. Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030. He will thus have spent 16 years in power, following his first stint as president from 2003 to 2010. Lula is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right. His options are also constrained by the economic outlook, with growth expected to slow. He has also come under renewed pressure to confront rampant insecurity in a country plagued by criminal factions that sow terror in working-class neighborhoods. The president’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States. Voters must “choose a country where the flag is respected,” he said, his raspy voice more hoarse than ever after a tireless campaign. He accused his rival of wanting to “govern with the American flag.” The post Brazil’s Lula clinches victory over Flavio Bolsonaro to win fourth term appeared first on Vanguard News .
